title: Nvidia Shield TV Pro is now $299 – a $100 price hike seven years after the Android TV box launched
snippet: The Nvidia Shield TV is an iconic piece of Android hardware but it also hasn’t seen a refresh in the better part of a decade. But, because of the increasingly depressing state of the entire tech industry, Nvidia Shield TV Pro is getting a $100 price hike to $299, seven years after it first launched. more…
fullText:
The Nvidia Shield TV is an iconic piece of Android hardware but it also hasn’t seen a refresh in the better part of a decade. But, because of the increasingly depressing state of the entire tech industry, Nvidia Shield TV Pro is getting a $100 price hike to $299, seven years after it first launched.

Nvidia Shield TV Pro made its debut in October 2019 and, to this day, remains one of the most capable Android TV streamers on the market. While certain aspects haven’t aged perfectly, such as a lack of AV1 support and others, it remains unmatched in other places.

That’s a big part of the reason that, even so many years after it launched, Nvidia continues to produce the Shield TV.

But the $199 price point is gone. Effective today, Nvidia Shield TV Pro now costs $299.99. Nvidia attributed the price hike to the fact that “the cost of components, including memory, has increased substantially across the industry.” Alongside the change in price, Nvidia has also ended production of the base Shield TV that was also introduced in 2019. The “tube” Shield has been out of stock for months at this point, but Shield TV Pro was just restocked at Best Buy.

	

Shield TV Pro at Best Buy

Early this year, Nvidia said that it would continue software support for the Shield TV for the forseeable future. 

Shield isn’t the only streamer going up in price as a result of RAMageddon. Google TV Streamer saw a price hike to $149 recently, while other devices including Apple TV 4K and various Roku streamers also saw price hikes earlier this year.

title: Trump’s ‘Super Intelligence’ AI Rebrand Has Everyone Shopping for Slovenia’s .SI Domain
snippet: Elon Musk says he will rename the just renamed SpaceXAI to SpaceXSI to align with the White House directive.
fullText:
Welcome to the dot-si boom? Less than two weeks after President Donald Trump declared that the US was officially renaming “artificial intelligence” to “super intelligence,” the domain extension .si has become a hot item around the world.

Elon Musk, who’s regained his trillionaire status, said he was renaming his AI company SpaceXAI to SpaceXSI, its second name change in less than three months.

Meanwhile, the central European country of Slovenia, whose official domain extension is .si, has registered more than 10,000 .si domain names every day since Wednesday. Slovenia allows anyone to obtain a .si domain name — you don’t have to live in the country. Coincidentally, First Lady Melania Trump is a native of Slovenia.

			

More from CNET

A domain extension, or top-level domain, is the set of letters after the final dot on a website address. Typically, these suffixes indicate the theme of the website, such as .gov for government, .edu for schools and .org for nonprofits, but there are country-specific domains as well. The most common extension is .com, followed by China’s .cn and Germany’s .de, according to digital services company CentralNic Reseller.

Web hosting provider Hostinger told TechCrunch that .si is now its second-most-popular domain extension after .com and that more than half of buyers are in the US and India.

Behind the .si surge

Trump announced in his speech to the UN on Sept. 22 that the US would begin using “super intelligence” to refer to AI in all official documents, saying, “The use of the word ‘artificial’ makes intelligence sound fake. It is not fake. It’s actually amazing.”

In a subsequent executive order titled Inaugurating the Era of Super Intelligence, Trump wrote that the new term “more appropriately captures the promise, potential, and rapidly advancing capabilities of these technologies.”

On Sunday, Trump announced his Super Intelligence Force, led by National Intelligence Director Jay Clayton. The small task force, Trump said, will focus on engagement with consumers, public interest groups, religious organizations, critical infrastructure providers and AI companies.

Trump was only 11 years old when the term “artificial intelligence” was coined in 1955 by computer scientist John McCarthy, who defined AI as “the science of making machines do things that would require intelligence if done by humans.”

Companies around the world have reacted to Trump’s announcement, scooping up .si domain names for future branding purposes. Other people are grabbing them with the idea that they could resell them to companies that want them. 

The domain name AI.si is now up for sale at nearly $700,000.

Register.si, Slovenia’s national registry and management platform for .si, says there were more than 46,000 domain registrations in September, a more than 15-fold increase from the 3,515 in August. The .si domain launched in September 2025. Register.si, run by the Academic and Research Network of Slovenia, charges registrars (like Hostinger) only about $11 per domain, which adds up to more than $300,000 in September.

Anguilla, a British territory in the Caribbean Sea, reaped more than $85 million last year from over 1 million registrations for the domain extension .ai, which the country controls.

Another Musk rebrand

Over the weekend, someone called X Freeze asked Musk on his social media site X (formerly Twitter), “Any possibility of renaming to SpaceXSI??,” to which Musk responded, “Yes, we will make that change.” As of this writing, the company is still listed as SpaceXAI on social media platforms and on its website.

In July, Musk renamed xAI to SpaceXAI after it was absorbed by the aerospace company in a $250 million acquisition in February. The company owns and operates the Grok chatbot and other Grok models and tools.

title: Google Home update rolling out with better ‘Find My Phone’ voice commands, smart home improvements
snippet: A new Google Home update has arrived with various improvements including better support for the “Find My Phone” voice command on Gemini speakers. more…
fullText:
A new Google Home update has arrived with various improvements including better support for the “Find My Phone” voice command on Gemini speakers.

In the Gemini for Home early access branch, Google says that users can expect “quality and reliability improvements” for the “Hey Google, find my phone” command that’s been around for years. It’s unclear exactly what’s changing, but this is a very useful voice command, so any upgrades will be welcome.

Improved Find My Phone reliability: Rolled out quality and reliability improvements to this fan-favorite feature when you ask Gemini to help locate your phone.

Other Gemini voice improvements in this latest update include filtering out background noise and voices, further speed/latency improvements, better support for multilingual households, and improved reliability to custom commands within Routines/automations.

In the Google Home app itself, there are quite a few updates to smart home functionality. This includes turning off lights when the brightness slider is dragged down to zero, improving camera and doorbell tiles, reducing Matter switches being incorrectly shown as offline, and improving setup for Nest devices.

	

Device Controller Enhancements

Accurate smart light shutoff: We’ve resolved an issue where sliding brightness down to 0% on single lights or group dimmers left bulbs powered on at minimum illumination instead of turning them off completely. Lowering your brightness to 0% now sends a definitive power-off command, preventing wasted energy and unexpected ambient glow.

Clearer online camera and doorbell tiles: Online cameras and doorbells now show as filled icons and accented tile colors at a glance, helping you instantly distinguish active cameras from idle ones.

Accurate offline switch status: We’ve resolved an issue where Matter switches failed to show their offline status or respond to taps on the All Devices tab, ensuring tiles properly render greyed out when disconnected.

Reliable Favorites tile gestures: We’ve resolved issues where long-pressing tiles in the Favorites tab failed to open device controllers or routine editors.

Smarter window covering detection: We’ve corrected device type resolution so awnings and curtains map accurately instead of defaulting all open-and-close window coverings to blinds.

Setup Improvements

Smoother smart device setup: We’ve delivered end-to-end reliability improvements when setting up Nest devices across iOS and Android. This includes under-the-hood fixes for Bluetooth connections and Wi-Fi pairing to eliminate common dropouts and stalls during the initial setup process.

Faster, standalone setup: When adding a new device to your home, the Google Home app can now securely cache network credentials on your mobile device, and reuse them for your next device.

There’s also a new preview option for Nest Doorbell ringtones.

The app update is rolling out now on Android, v4.31.27.1, while the Gemini updates are happening behind the scenes for those in early access.

title: Reddit is making two changes some long-time users won’t like
snippet: Reddit has announced two upcoming changes which are likely to prove unpopular with some long-time users. The company has already placed one restriction on Old Reddit, and it has now announced a second one. Additionally, RSS support is being discontinued … more…
fullText:
Reddit has announced two upcoming changes which are likely to prove unpopular with some long-time users.

The company has already placed one restriction on Old Reddit, and it has now announced a second one. Additionally, RSS support is being discontinued … 

Old Reddit

Reddit significantly changed its user interface way back in 2018, sparking significant objections from those who preferred the original version. To address this, the platform said that it would continue to provide access to what has become known as Old Reddit for as long as people kept using it.

The first change to this policy came in August of this year when the company required Old Reddit users to be logged in. It has now announced that the original UI will be limited to those who have used it within the last six months, denying access to new users.

In the next few months, we’ll further limit access for logged-in users to only those who have used Old Reddit in the last six months (which covers the vast majority of all Old Reddit users).

Reddit says that both moves were made to reduce AI scraping by companies (though this is apparently fine if they pay for the privilege).

The same rationale has been cited for discontinuing RSS feeds.

Because RSS is now a common surface for large-scale scraping and automated abuse, we’ll stop supporting RSS feeds on November 13, 2026.

This could be particularly problematic for subreddits who rely on these for moderation workflows. Reddit says it is aware of this and is recommending moderators use Devvit apps like Discord Relay.

Users unimpressed

Reading the comments in the thread, it’s clear that a lot of long-time users are very unhappy about the latest developments.

They said Old Reddit wasn’t going away, but Reddit lies all the time […] They’ll keep messing with stuff until they turn the site into a Twitter/Facebook hybrid and everyone except the Facebook/Twitter crowd abandons them.

fullText:
Good morning and happy October. Today, I’m cringing at this gaggle of billionaires pretending to be human, vibing to the new Tinashe album, Popstar, and heartily dining on all the brutal ‘Digger’ reviews.

As a reminder, Inbox is the tech newsletter that goes beyond the news cycle. We cover the most important 9to5Google stories from the last couple of days along with a few highlights from around the web. We publish every Tuesday and Thursday, and if you like what you read, please subscribe.

Inbox is written by Daniel Bader. Read previous issues here, and then catch up with Ben Schoon’s excellent Weekender column published every Sunday.

⭐️ Starred

What year is it?

	

After months of waiting, Gemini 4 ‘Argon’ is finally out — sort of. Google unveiled the new state-of-the-art model late yesterday but has only made it available to “a set of trusted cyber defenders” while it undergoes testing. The company says it will get a wider release “as soon as possible.”

This is a big moment for Google. Many users and critics alike wrote it off completely, with one analysis firm saying “for all intents and purposes, we believe DeepMind is no longer a frontier lab.” While the company has released several useful, fast and affordable Flash-branded models in 2026, its latest salvo into state-of-the-art AI was back in November 2025 with Gemini 3 Pro. In fact, it was so good that for a brief time Google was considered to be well ahead of OpenAI and Anthropic, and presaged a “code red” inside the frontier labs.

It’s hard to overstate how important it is for Gemini 4 to succeed. After a massive executive shuffle in August saw Demis Hassabis and Jeff Dean removed from the core management team, most of DeepMind’s operations were shifted from London to Mountain View, where new head Koray Kavukcuoglu reports directly to Google CEO Sundar Pichai.

While there has been speculation that Google, with its entrenched customer base, would walk away from the frontier in favor of cheaper, more product-focused pursuits, Kavukcuoglu has refuted those rumors. Earlier this month, he said, “To put it very bluntly, there’s nothing other than being at the frontier that is important for us. We have the whole full stack… and we are able to optimize to be able to achieve our goals.”

According to benchmarks, Gemini 4 is competitive with GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus 5.5 in most tests, and is trained to be much better at agentic tasks than any previous Gemini model. It’s also better aligned, with a focus on cybersecurity, and has a massive 1M token output limit, which makes it far more capable of producing large bodies of work in one prompt with less compaction.

The big question, though, is whether Argon will be competitive in the real world. A Bloomberg report published shortly before the embargo lifted on the Gemini 4 news quoted anonymous Google employees skeptical of its coding abilities. From Bloomberg: “While Gemini 4 has performed well on benchmarks widely used to gauge model efficacy, it does less well when employees actually put it to work, according to people with direct access to the effort. The model struggles to handle certain coding tasks, said the people, who requested anonymity to discuss an internal matter.”

Argon is also curiously priced. Its introductory rate of $2/$10 per million input/output tokens matches OpenAI’s Sol 6.1 cost right now, but will eventually double to hit the $4/$20 price of Claude Opus 5.5. While still significantly cheaper than Astra or Fable, it has to prove its mettle with users before Google is welcomed back into the arms of the fickle AI masses.

title: Etched fields funding offers at $40B+ valuation, sources say
snippet: Just a couple of months after its last big raise, the AI chip startup is already being plied with investment offers at double or more its current value, sources tell TechCrunch.
fullText:
Although it’s only been a couple of months since Etched raised $700 million at a $21 billion valuation, the AI chip startup is already being plied with investment offers at double or more its value, according to people familiar with the company.

Etched is reviewing incoming bids that range from $40 billion from top-tier investors to $50 billion from lesser-known backers, one person said. These fundraising talks are early, so terms of any deal, should one happen, may change. Etched declined to comment.

While this may seem like a fast timetable to raise another mega round, Etched is pursuing a particularly expensive segment of the AI industry: building full AI hardware systems powered by its own proprietary chips. The person familiar with these offers said that if it raises as much as its last round, this could give Etched a cushion of as much as 3.5 years of runway.

There are reasons why VCs are hot to own a piece of Etched. The four-year-old startup shows promise of challenging Nvidia. Not only did quant trading firm Jane Street lead the last $700 million round, it is also a customer that took delivery of an early system. Etched said in July that it had already secured $1 billion in customer orders, including the one from Jane Street, after manufacturing its test chip at a TSMC factory this summer.

Co-founder and COO Robert Wachen previously told TechCrunch that investors are so enthusiastic because Etched has designed two new components from scratch to speed up inference — the computing process that happens after a user submits a prompt.  

The company claims its chips can process more tokens faster and at a lower cost than Nvidia’s. That’s the reason its processors have been so attractive to Jane Street, for whom a microscopic advantage in speed can yield massive profits.

The startup has also impressed investors with its ability to attract engineers from Nvidia, with roughly 15% of Etched’s 400-person workforce having previously worked at the chip giant, according to The Wall Street Journal.

Etched also operates a new 10-megawatt data center in Silicon Valley and established a facility in Taiwan to coordinate production near TSMC.

Co-founders Gavin Uberti and Chris Zhu famously met in an advanced math course at Harvard, while Wachen was Uberti’s roommate and they dropped out to pursue the company. 

In terms of fast rounds at big leaps in valuations, Etched already has a history of them. The startup announced a $300 million round at a $10.3 billion valuation led by Sequoia in July. It announced the $700 million round at a $21 billion valuation in September. Back-to-back funding rounds, which essentially act as a single financing split into two tranches with separate valuations, are increasingly common among the buzziest startups.

title: Google Play adding Usage-Based Billing subscriptions aimed at AI apps
snippet: Google Play today is giving Android developers more payment options around subscriptions, including Usage-Based Billing. more…
fullText:
Google Play today is giving Android developers more payment options around subscriptions, including Usage-Based Billing.

Google says the “subscription landscape is evolving rapidly” due to generative AI and “increasingly sophisticated app experiences.” 

End users should be on the lookout for Usage-Based Billing to support generative AI apps and other usage-based services. This “prepaid metered billing” works by letting users “automatically top up their balance whenever it falls below a set threshold.” 

For large groups like businesses and schools, there’s Multi-Quantity Subscription Purchase. Organizations can “make multiple subscription purchases in a single transaction and easily assign those as seats or subscriptions to team members or students.”

	

Mixed Carts allow developers to sell auto-renewing subscriptions and one-time products at the same time. For example:

This unified experience also opens up powerful upsell opportunities for your business—such as offering targeted discounts if an end user purchases a complete bundle of a subscription and complementary in-app items together.

Cross-Developer Bundling lets developers “create and sell a hard bundle of two or more complementary subscriptions in your own catalog.” The example Google gives is bundling a language-learning app with a travel guide service for a “combined subscription at a discounted rate.”

This capability allows you to team up with other developers—or combine offerings across your own portfolio of apps—to deliver massive value through a single purchase.

These Play Store features are “currently available or rolling out through [Google’s] Early Access Program.”

title: Texas school district ditches Chromebooks, approves $11M iPad and MacBook Neo deal
snippet: A Texas school district is going all-in on the iPad and MacBook Neo as part of a new $11 million deal. The Beaumont Independent School District is ditching its Chromebook fleet and opting for Apple gear going forward, citing better reliability, lower costs, and performance. As reported by the Beaumont Enterprise this week, the Beaumont Independent School District’s board has approved an $11.19 million four-year lease to upgrade its technology ecosystem. more…
fullText:
A Texas school district is going all-in on the iPad and MacBook Neo as part of a new $11 million deal. The Beaumont Independent School District is ditching its Chromebook fleet and opting for Apple gear going forward, citing better reliability, lower costs, and performance.

As reported by the Beaumont Enterprise this week, the Beaumont Independent School District’s board has approved an $11.19 million four-year lease to upgrade its technology ecosystem.

As part of the deal, the school district will provide 14,585 Apple devices to teachers and students from pre-K through 12th grade. The new Apple gear will replace an aging collection of Chromebooks, many purchased more than five years ago. The district was spending nearly half a million dollars on repairs and support for that Chromebook fleet.

The new initiative includes more than 4,000 iPads for students pre-K through second grade and 9,500 MacBook Neo units for third through 12th grade students. The district also allocated 1,000 MacBook Neo devices for teachers.

The district compared the MacBook Neo to products from Lenovo and Asus and ultimately concluded the MacBook Neo had the “strongest performance and reliability among the devices evaluated.” Apple’s financing terms were also more favorable. Access to AppleCare also influenced the decision.

From the report:

According to the district’s comparison, the Lenovo model had a minimum financing rate of 4%, a higher four-year cost and a guaranteed buyback value of $10 per device. The Asus model had competitive upfront pricing and met instructional needs but also cost more over four years. The district said the Asus model’s plastic parts would require more repairs.

title: Here’s everything we know so far about Apple’s next entry-level iPad: A19 chip, more
snippet: Apple’s current iPad, the A16 model, has gone untouched for well over a year. It remains the only device in Apple’s core product lineup without support for Apple Intelligence. Rumors had swirled for quite some time about an A18 model coming this year. Now, it’s sounding like Apple has an even bigger plan. more…
fullText:
Apple’s current iPad, the A16 model, has gone untouched for well over a year. It remains the only device in Apple’s core product lineup without support for Apple Intelligence. Rumors had swirled for quite some time about an A18 model coming this year. Now, it’s sounding like Apple has an even bigger plan.

It’s likely safe to assume that the delays with this product launch have much to do with the ongoing memory crisis affecting the electronics industry. It wouldn’t surprise me if Apple had the A18 refresh roadmapped for earlier this year alongside the debut of the M4 iPad Air, then had to push it.

As a reminder, Apple raised the price of the base iPad from $349 to $449 this summer alongside the rest of its memory-related price hikes. This brings it back to the price it initially launched at in 2022.

New iPad details

However, a new leak from MacRumors contributor Aaron Perris paints a more promising picture. Instead of utilizing the A18 chip, it sounds like the next entry-level iPad will equip the A19 chip. Alongside that, you’ll get the N1 networking chip, as well as the C1X modem on the cellular version. This’ll bring support for Wi-Fi 7 to Apple’s cheapest iPad.

The A19 iPad will also be equipped with 8GB of memory, allowing users to run Siri AI, though you’ll still miss out on the most capable local models and the more advanced dictation models, as those features require 12GB of memory. It’s not a major loss, but worth pointing out.

Another possibility is that the A19 iPad might offer a new name. With the debut of the MacBook Neo, Apple marketing exec Greg Joswiak pointed out that calling the MacBook Neo just “MacBook” would leave it without an identity. Hopefully, with the next entry-level iPad, we also get some sort of proper name like “SE” or “Neo” so we have something to call it.

Beyond that, don’t expect any sort of redesign or display improvements. There may be new colors, but probably nothing else. I personally wish Apple would bring USB 3 to the product, so users don’t have to suffer with such slow transfer speeds. It’d certainly help justify the new higher starting price.

Release date

	

Apple’s next budget iPad should be releasing next Spring, per Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman. That’ll accompany other products like the M6 MacBook Air, A19 Pro MacBook Neo, M7 14-inch MacBook Pro, and more.

Are you someone in the market for the entry-level iPad? What are you most looking forward to? Let us know in the comments.

title: Mistral’s new 1T model aims to leapfrog closed and open rivals
snippet: French AI lab Mistral AI has released Mistral Large 4, a new large multimodal model aiming to leapfrog both American and Chinese rivals.
fullText:
The race between open and closed AI is on, and Europe is still in the mix. On Tuesday, French AI lab Mistral AI released Mistral Large 4 (ML4), a new large multimodal model aiming to leapfrog both American and Chinese rivals — following what French president Macron described as “a third way in AI.”

Amid a growing divide between closed models that can be unplugged and open models that are often made in China, Mistral is positioning ML4 as an alternative to both. Nicknamed Le Chonk in reference to its 1 trillion parameters, ML4 is definitely not small; but is not an open-weight model yet. For the time being, it can only be accessed via a public guardrail endpoint, but Mistral plans to make its weights available in just three weeks, after safety testing is complete.

“In the meantime, we’ll work with trusted partners and governments to make sure that the open source weights can be used to defend, but not to [perform] malicious attacks,” Mistral VP Science Pierre Stock told TechCrunch. 

Security concerns have been mounting in recent months, particularly among Mistral’s core audience —  enterprises and institutions. At the same time, an open-weight model is easier to audit, Stock said.

Another important behind-the-scenes aspect is that ML4 was trained entirely on Mistral’s compute; using only 4,000 Nvidia GPUs “which is two to three times less than our Chinese competitors, and significantly less than the closed source competitors,” Stock said.

With benchmark results still pending, Mistral hopes ML4 will be best in class among open-weight models, especially outside of China, but not only, Stock said. Thanks to focused training, it could also outperform closed models in specific areas that are key to its customers, and where multimodal capabilities can add value.

According to Stock, ML4’s optimized use cases include cybersecurity and finance, but also chip design, which is core to two of Mistral’s main backers — Dutch giant ASML, which led its Series C, and Samsung, which led its Series D last month at a €21 billion valuation (about $24.39 billion).

At the time, the company tried to convey that its decision to host Chinese models wasn’t a pivot into becoming a mere inference provider. With Le Chonk in its corner, the company believes it should still be considered a frontier lab as well.

title: Get all your questions answered at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026: The full breakout session agenda revealed
snippet: Get all of your scaling and tech questions answered at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026. Here's the full breakout session agenda, happening October 13-15 in San Francisco. Register now to join and save up to $100, and get a second pass at 50% off.
fullText:
TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 lands at Moscone West in San Francisco on October 13-15, bringing together 10,000+ founders, investors, operators, and tech leaders for three days of ideas, connections, and conversations about what’s coming next. This year’s lineup gets into the questions founders and operators are dealing with right now: How do you build with AI agents? Where will value accrue as AI shifts from training to inference? What does physical AI really mean? How do you run a better fundraiser? And how does AI change the way you grow companies and teams?

Get into the room, get your questions answered, and make the connections that’ll spark your next move in the ecosystem. Save up to $100 on your pass and 50% on a second. Bring a group of four-plus to save more and get more insights. If you’ve recently been laid off, get a $75 Expo+ Pass before they run out.

The complete Disrupt 2026 breakout session agenda

Get to know the sessions and tech leaders shaping the conversation on the Disrupt agenda.

What Is Physical AI, Anyway? 

Susan Schofer, Partner and Chief Science Officer, SOSV HAX; and Duncan Turner, General Partner and Managing Director, SOSV HAX

Sponsored by SOSV

AI is moving beyond software and into machines that need to perceive, reason, and act in unpredictable environments. Schofer and Turner break down what actually qualifies as physical AI, why building it requires a different playbook, and what investors are looking for in companies trying to define the category.

Outnumbered Either Way: How an Engineer and an Architect Run Their Jobs on Agents

Steve Androulakis and Sachin Malhotra, Members of Technical Staff, Anthropic

What does an AI-agent workflow look like when the people using it build AI for a living? Anthropic’s Androulakis and Malhotra show how they run multiple Claude agents in parallel, delegate real engineering work, review output, recover when agents get things wrong, and make agents part of their everyday jobs.

How to build AI we can trust

Robbie Goldfarb, Co-founder, Forum AI

As AI takes on more consequential work, accuracy alone isn’t enough. Drawing on experience spanning misinformation, online safety, and work with foundation-model labs, Goldfarb explores how expert human judgment can become scalable evaluations — and what it will take to build AI systems people can actually rely on.

The Inference Economy: Why AI’s Next Trillion Dollars Won’t Look Like Its First

Hagay Lupesko, SVP, AI Cloud, Cerebras Systems; and Rudina Seseri, Founder and Managing Partner, Glasswing Ventures

As frontier models become increasingly commoditized, AI’s economics are shifting from training toward inference. This session looks at where defensibility comes from when the model itself isn’t the moat, why latency is becoming part of the product, and what those changes mean for infrastructure decisions, startup economics, and what investors will look for next.

Building Then vs Now

Dr. Rumman Chowdhury, CEO and Co-founder, Humane Intelligence; Payal Kadakia, Founder, ClassPass; Cassie Kozyrkov, Founder, Kozyr; and Holly Ransom, CEO, Emergent

Sponsored by Signify Business Cash World Elite Mastercard by Wells Fargo

The fundamentals of building a company may not have changed, but the tools certainly have. Leaders spanning AI, data, entrepreneurship, and strategy examine how founders can use AI to make better decisions and move faster — while understanding where bias, judgment, and the human side of company building still matter.

Best Practices for Running a Successful Fundraise: From Preparation to Investor Engagement 

Speakers to be announced

Sponsored by Fidelity Private Shares

A successful fundraise starts long before the pitch. This interactive session takes founders through the process from both sides of the table, covering investor targeting, relationship building, outreach, maintaining momentum, cap tables, data rooms, and due diligence. Come away with practical ways to run a more organized and effective raise.

Image Credits:TechCrunch / Slava Blazer Photography

From Founder to Investor: The Next Act – What Happens After You Win?

Bruce K Lee, CEO and Founder, Keebeck Wealth Management; and Abhi Tiwari, Co-founder and General Partner, Blank Ventures

Building and funding a company requires one mindset. Becoming an investor requires another. Lee and Tiwari explore what happens when entrepreneurs move from raising capital to allocating it — and why founders may want to start thinking about their post-exit strategy long before an exit actually happens. 

Breaking Into Space: The AI Builder’s Opportunity 

Dr. Brian Cameron, Interim Chief Technology Officer, The Aerospace Corporation; Bosco Lai, CEO, Little Place Labs; and Shawn Sloan, Corporate Fellow for Artificial Intelligence, The Aerospace Corporation

Sponsored by The Aerospace Corporation

Space may look like a specialist market, but many of its problems will feel familiar to AI builders: huge data streams, autonomous decisions, real-time processing, and complex agent systems. This session maps those capabilities to real space applications and shows founders where new commercial and government opportunities are opening up.

Fundraising Mistakes That Will Kill Your Round, and How to Avoid Them 

Dr. Irena King, Founder and CEO, Surgicure Technologies; Dr. Richard Munassi, Accelerator Managing Director and Chief Strategy Officer, Tampa Bay Wave; Ashley Paston, Partner, General Catalyst; and Emily Zhen, Principal, HealthQuest Capital

Sponsored by Tampa Bay Wave

Great companies can still run bad fundraising processes. This session gets into the mistakes that derail rounds, from positioning and preparation to investor strategy and execution. Expect practical lessons, real examples, and a clearer framework for taking your next raise from the first pitch through to close.

Building a Growth Engine in the AI Era: Lessons from a Bootstrapped Unicorn 

Patrick Burke, Managing Director, Hostinger

Sponsored by Hostinger

AI is compressing the distance between spotting an opportunity and acting on it. Using examples from Hostinger, Burke explores how startups can identify underpriced distribution channels, shorten the loop between market signals and product launches, experiment faster, and put agentic marketing workflows to work to drive growth.

Physical AI Isn’t a Model Problem. It’s an Execution Problem.

Ethan Batraski, Partner, Venrock; Ivan Poupyrev, Founder and CEO, Archetype AI; and Ian Rountree, General Partner, Cantos

The real physical AI opportunity isn’t simply understanding the world — it’s acting in it. Builders and investors explore the execution layer between perception, decision, action, and verification, and why the companies that can reliably close that loop could become some of the most durable businesses in industrial AI.

Talent as the Operating System: How High-Performance Teams Scale in the AI Era

AI can change how work gets done, but companies still depend on people, trust, and execution. Khedawala explores how leaders can build stronger alignment across teams, spot breakdowns before they become bigger problems, and create systems that support accountability and sustainable high performance as organizations scale.

title: iOS 27’s Siri gets one thing very right that other AI assistants get wrong
snippet: Siri AI is a major upgrade to Apple’s assistant that’s now available in iOS 27. And there’s one standout area I’ve noticed where it differs greatly from other AI assistants—for the better. more…
fullText:
Siri AI is a major upgrade to Apple’s assistant that’s now available in iOS 27. And there’s one standout area I’ve noticed where it differs greatly from other AI assistants—for the better.

iOS 27’s new Siri doesn’t pretend to be human, unlike every other AI chatbot

I’ve been using Siri AI for nearly four months, since the first iOS 27 beta launched. Overall, it’s checked all the boxes I was hoping for.

The new Siri is far more capable than its predecessor, delivering on the original promise of being a truly capable assistant on Apple devices.

I’ll admit though: if you need the most powerful, cutting-edge AI tool, you might be better served by competitors like ChatGPT, Claude, and Google Gemini.

However, after using Siri AI and comparing it to those third-party tools, I’ve noticed a key difference where I greatly favor Siri.

Unlike other AI chatbots, Siri doesn’t pretend to be human.

It’s not overly verbose, mimicking a human-like personality that might lull you into forming a personal relationship with it.

Siri is helpful, intelligent, and does what you ask it to do. But the way it responds makes clear that it’s a tool, not a person. It reminds you regularly that it’s an AI, so it can make mistakes. And it won’t faux date you.

Whereas ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini are all bursting with personality, opinions, and demonstrate more human-like tendencies in a way that, for me, feels disingenuous.

I imagine some users enjoy that more “personal” approach. But I much prefer that AI assistants stay in their lane and don’t pretend to be something they’re not.

AI is changing the world. But AI chatbots are tools, not people. And I love that Apple gets that, and built the new Siri accordingly.

What’s your view of how “human-like” an AI assistant should be? Let us know in the comments.

title: Google stands by Gemini 4 performance as some claim it ‘struggles’ in real-world use
snippet: Google yesterday unveiled its new flagship Gemini 4 model with some impressive scores, but a report suggests that it might “struggle” in some cases. more…
fullText:
Google yesterday unveiled its new flagship Gemini 4 model with some impressive scores, but a report suggests that it might “struggle” in some cases.

Google announces Gemini 4 Argon as its new frontier model

Bloomberg reports that, internally, Google employees have found that Gemini 4’s real-world performance doesn’t always line up with its benchmark scores. During the unveiling of Gemini 4 Argon, Google showed that its new model outpaced competitors including OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra in many key areas.

The report cites Googlers who found that the model “does less well when employees actually put it to work,” and that it “struggles to handle certain coding tasks.” Google, speaking to Bloomberg on the claims, said that it “would be inaccurate to say that Gemini 4 is underperforming in areas such as coding,” also referencing comments from Koray Kavukcuoglu, the head of Google DeepMind, from late September, when he said that “it’s a certainty that we are always gonna be at the frontier.” The report cites one Googler who said that there’s a “large consensus” that Gemini 4 is at the frontier amongst employees, while others are concerned that Gemini “will still lag behind” competing models from Anthropic and OpenAI. Clearly, there’s a split in how employees view the model’s performance.

Gemini 4 Argon brings welcome upgrades to the model, including an expanded output limit of up to 1 million tokens, while Google also explained that the model is “highly capable at cybersecurity defense” and shows “leading performance” in other use cases. Gemini 4 Argon comes at a cost of “$4 per 1M input tokens and $20 per 1M output tokens” but will see introductory pricing which is half of that.

title: Uber is spending $2.3B to get into catering
snippet: It's the latest in a string of deals meant to grow Uber Eats into a food delivery behemoth.
fullText:
In Brief

Posted:

7:00 AM PDT · October 6, 2026

Image Credits:Jakub Porzycki/NurPhoto / Getty Images

		

							

											
									

					

	

Uber is buying a catering company called ezCater, as it continues to grow the types of services available through its Uber Eats division. It’s an all-cash transaction valued at $2.3 billion.

Billed as a “leading U.S. platform for catering and workplace meals,” ezCater is a marketplace for businesses that need large meals, like an Expedia for catering. The company was founded in 2007 and has become a business that generated over $2.5 billion in gross bookings over the last 12 months, according to Uber. It’s a huge exit for a company that was bootstrapped for seven years before raising its first $4 million round in 2014.

Dara Khosrowshahi, Uber’s CEO, billed the acquisition as a way for restaurants to find new, larger customers. “Catering is a big business, and can be a huge revenue stream for restaurants,” he said in a statement. “With Uber’s reach, we can bring that experience to millions more customers and help restaurants win more of these valuable orders.”

The acquisition is the latest in a run of moves by Uber to grow its food delivery business. The company is also in the process of buying Delivery Hero for $15 billion, and it’s investing in (and partnering with) drone delivery companies like Zipline and Flytrex.

title: HBO Max and Paramount+ set to merge under ‘Skydance’ brand
snippet: Paramount Skydance will complete its acquisition of Warner Bros. next week, and CEO David Ellison just revealed ‘Skydance’ as the new company name ahead of a planned merging of HBO Max and Paramount+ streaming services. more…
fullText:
Paramount Skydance will complete its acquisition of Warner Bros. next week, and CEO David Ellison just revealed ‘Skydance’ as the new company name ahead of a planned merging of HBO Max and Paramount+ streaming services.

‘Skydance’ is name of merged Paramount-Warner Bros. company, and likely name of merged streaming service too

Warner Bros. Discovery is officially set to be merged with Paramount Skydance next Tuesday, October 6.

Following a lengthy approval process and recent settlement, and after beating out Netflix’s initial deal for WBD, the owner of Paramount+ will merge with the owner of HBO Max. 

And the new name for this merged company? Skydance.

CEO David Ellison just joined X and made the name announcement in his first post.

What once was the peak, is now just the beginning.

Paramount and Warner Bros. shaped over a century of culture. By combining them, we aren't rewriting history — we're equipping these iconic studios with a more powerful engine. Together, we are Skydance: a creative-first home for… pic.twitter.com/uInLRY3IrE

— David Ellison (@ellisonskydance) October 2, 2026

	

Earlier this year, when asked about plans for HBO Max and Paramount+ if the merger went through, Ellison said the streamers would be combined into a single service. Per CNBC:

Paramount+ and HBO Max will be combined into one streaming service if regulators approve Paramount Skydance’s acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery, Paramount CEO David Ellison said on a conference call Monday. A combined service would have about 200 million subscribers given existing totals, Ellison said during his company’s investor call about the WBD transaction. […]

Paramount executives didn’t offer any details Monday on how the company may price a combined service or what it would be called. Still, Ellison said he wouldn’t disrupt the HBO brand. “HBO should stay HBO,” he said, citing its long history of quality programming. HBO is likely to be a sub-brand within the larger service, according to a person familiar with Paramount’s plans.

Now that Skydance is the official name for the merged company, there’s a very good chance it will become the name of the new, combined streaming service too.

There’s been no timeline communicated yet for HBO Max and Paramount+ to merge, but we may get those details next week after the merger closes.

title: Samsung has updated these Galaxy devices to Android 17
snippet: Samsung is now rolling out its Android 17-based update, One UI 9, to its collection of supported Galaxy smartphones and tablets. Here’s the full list of devices that have been updated so far, and what you should know about the update. more…
fullText:
Samsung is now rolling out its Android 17-based update, One UI 9, to its collection of supported Galaxy smartphones and tablets. Here’s the full list of devices that have been updated so far, and what you should know about the update.

What’s new in Android 17 on Samsung Galaxy?

One UI 9, Samsung’s Android 17 update, continues the trend of evolution more than overhaul. The update introduces some slight design tweaks, more AI-powered features, and other changes built on the redesign that debuted in One UI 7 and was iterated in last year’s Android 16-based One UI 8. 

Some key changes in One UI 9 include:

Warranty & Samsung Care status in the Settings menu

Broader support for Now Nudge

My FanCam automatic video cropping based on a select subject

More Quick Panel (quick settings) customization

AI privacy alerts

Upgrades to Samsung DeX

New lock screen clocks that can adapt to your wallpaper

Samsung Galaxy devices with Android 17 – The full list

While Samsung hasn’t confirmed an exact schedule for its One UI 9 and Android 17 rollout for Galaxy devices, there are updates now rolling out in parts of the globe. Below you’ll find a regularly-updated list of every Samsung Galaxy device that has received a stable Android 17 update so far.

Updating…

One UI 9 changelog

Here’s the full changelog from Samsung for One UI 9, as listed for the Galaxy S26 series. Some features may vary by device.

Galaxy AI

Enhanced Now nudge

Now nudge provides helpful suggestions in more places throughout your Galaxy experience. In addition to the keyboard, suggestions will now appear in conversation notifications and in a floating button in the bottom right corner of the screen. There are also several new types of suggestions, like entering reservation details or addresses and saving places in Google Maps.

Focus on someone important

My FanCam lets you select a person in a video and follow them automatically while cropping out the rest of the video.

Interpreter keeps your conversation in front of you

In conversation mode, you can scroll through the whole conversation while you’re still talking.

See useful information during calls

See relevant events and other information related to your current call on the call screen.

Productivity and multitasking

More customizable quick panel

You can now rearrange and customize the controls in your quick panel even more than before. You can change the size of the brightness and volume sliders as well as the media player. You can also separate the sound mode button from the volume slider.

Privacy, security, and device protection

Warranty and care

The new Warranty and care menu in settings lets you check your warranty information and access diagnostic checks and useful information for keeping your Galaxy in top condition.

Lock down your phone quickly

It’s now easier to securely lock your phone in a hurry. Just press and hold the Volume down and Side buttons at the same time or tap the Power button in the quick panel. This prevents biometrics from being used the next time you unlock your phone.

Location access transparency

Stay on top of your location privacy. A blue indicator will appear at the top of the screen when an app accesses your location. Tap the indicator in the quick panel to see which app it is.

Stronger security and privacy protection

Alerts will appear in your Now brief to let you know about risks from malware, apps from unknown sources, unnecessary permissions, and other issues that may put your security and privacy at risk. Apps that have been identified as malicious or vulnerable will be blocked from opening until you make a decision about whether to remove them.

AI privacy alerts

Get help protecting your personal data. AI will monitor how apps use permissions and notify you about unnecessary access to your personal data.

Samsung Health

New look for Samsung Health

Samsung Health has been redesigned to make your health data easier to understand. Enjoy clearer visuals, improved charts, and a more engaging experience to help you reach your health goals.

Customize your Health home screen

Resize cards and organize them by category, like Activity, Sleep, Mindfulness, and Nutrition, so your top priorities are easy to access.

Log health data quickly

It’s now easier to add your health information right from the Samsung Health home screen. You can log your mood, meals, and more. You can even use the camera for faster input.

Advanced trend analysis

Track your progress with improved trend charts in Samsung Health. View data in hourly, daily, or weekly intervals, pinch to zoom in for a closer look, and overlay multiple charts to compare your performance across different periods.

Monitor changes in your sleep vitals

Samsung Health helps you notice meaningful changes in your sleep health data. Use Galaxy Watch or Ring measurements to better understand your daily health patterns.

Manage your heart health

Track key health metrics and lifestyle factors that affect your heart. A daily score based on your sleep, exercise, BMI, and blood pressure helps you better understand your current heart health trends.

Track your cardio load

See how your workouts and activity impact your heart so you’ll know when to push harder and when to rest. Your target cardio load range adjusts daily based on your recent activity and training focus.

Check your fitness index

Your Fitness Index is an overall score calculated using five key fitness metrics: body composition, cardio, strength, flexibility, and endurance. Set a goal and unlock personalized insights tailored to your results.

Keep your ears safe

The new Hearing tracker monitors sound levels detected by your Galaxy Watch and headphone audio levels to help you manage your exposure to loud sounds.

View your cycle and body rhythm

Get a more personalized view of your cycle and body rhythm with new cycle tracking options. You can view your cycle information in your calendar and better understand your health patterns.

Bixby

Activate Bixby with a gesture

Talk to Bixby just by raising your phone close to your mouth and speaking. No wake-up word needed.

Manage your conversations

Keep your chats organized. Search them, rename them, or pin your favorites. You can also delete all of your past conversations at once.

Bixby on the Home screen

Add a Bixby widget to type or talk to Bixby or jump directly to your conversation history.

Accessibility

Discover new Accessibility features

Check the What’s new menu in Accessibility settings to learn about and try the latest Accessibility features for your Galaxy.

Text spotlight for easier reading

Need a closer look? Tap any text on the screen to show it enlarged and highlighted in its own window. You can also customize the font size, colors, and other settings to match your preferences.

Physical keyboard shortcuts

Use shortcuts on your physical keyboard to access the Accessibility settings you need without touching the screen.

Mouse keys enhancements

New options are available when using your keyboard for mouse interactions including speed and acceleration control. You can also use the keyboard’s number pad to point and click.

Replace swipe with single tap

The Replace swipe with single tap option is now located in the Dexterity and interaction menu instead of the Assistant menu for easier access.

Select to speak

Get quick audio readouts without turning on full TalkBack. With the new Select to speak feature, you can select an item on your screen, like text or an image, and hear it read or described out loud.

Improved TalkBack updates

TalkBack updates can now be applied with a simple app update from the Play Store, helping you get the latest accessibility features and enhancements.

Even more improvements

New Lock screen clock

The default clock on your Lock screen has been redesigned with a cleaner and more modern look that adapts to match your wallpaper.

Samsung DeX enhancements

It’s easier to move an app window from one desktop to another using the menu at the top of the window. Desktop previews are now available at the top of the Recents screen, making it easier to switch with a single tap.

title: Paramount closes historic Warner Bros. merger to form Skydance
snippet: The deal brings together two major streaming platforms, Paramount+ and HBO Max, along with networks including CBS, CNN, MTV, TBS, Comedy Central, and Food Network.
fullText:
Paramount announced on Tuesday that it has completed its $110 billion acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery to create a combined company called Skydance. 

The deal, which is one of the biggest mergers of all time, brings together two major streaming platforms, Paramount+ and HBO Max, along with networks including CBS, CNN, MTV, TBS, Comedy Central, and Food Network. Skydance will also gain control of major franchises such as “The Lord of the Rings,” “Game of Thrones,” the DC Universe, and “Yellowstone.”

The merger puts one of the world’s largest entertainment studios under the control of David Ellison. Just last year, Ellison completed his merger of Skydance Media with Paramount, and is rapidly increasing his influence in Hollywood.

The Ellison family is Skydance’s largest shareholder, backed by the billions of Larry Ellison, David Ellison’s father and co-founder of Oracle.

The completion of the deal comes after settlements with a coalition of U.S. states and a Hollywood writers’ union cleared the main legal hurdles facing the merger. 

Paramount announced in February that it would acquire Warner Bros. following a bidding battle with Netflix, which had previously reached an agreement to purchase Warner Bros.’ film and television studios and streaming business, excluding its cable networks.

Paramount had sweetened its bid by promising shareholders additional cash if the deal failed to close by a specified deadline and agreeing to cover the breakup fee Warner Bros. would owe Netflix for ending its existing agreement.

“Today is a historic day, not just for Skydance but for our entire industry,” Ellison said in a statement. “From the start, our ambition was to bring these two storied studios together and create a stronger competitor, with the talent, resources, and reach to tell great stories in every genre, on every platform, for audiences everywhere. Our focus now turns to the future: building a company that empowers creatives, entertains audiences and rewards shareholders. We couldn’t be more excited to get to work.”

The new combined Skydance corporation will have annual revenue of nearly $70 billion, the company says.

Skydance Class B shares will begin trading on the New York Stock Exchange today under the ticker symbol “SKYD.”

title: Some Pixel models reportedly experiencing an NFC bug that breaks contactless payments
snippet: Following several Pixel 11-specific bugs after the phone’s launch, another one reportedly breaks NFC tap-to-pay, used for contactless payments. But this one is affecting more than just the Pixel 11. more…
fullText:
Following several Pixel 11-specific bugs after the phone’s launch, another one reportedly breaks NFC tap-to-pay, used for contactless payments. But this one is affecting more than just the Pixel 11.

A slew of reports on Reddit have been posted within the last two weeks regarding a new Google Pixel bug that affects NFC payments (via Android Authority). Users have been reporting that their Pixel devices can no longer use tap-to-pay, whether directly in the Google Wallet app or at automatic transit terminals that don’t require the app to be open.

The issue isn’t affecting just the Pixel 11, so this can’t be piled onto the list of device-specific issues users are coming across – of which there are a good few. The Reddit posts and comments within list Google Pixel models ranging from the Pixel 8 to the new Pixel 11 Pro XL. The bug is agnostic to model or series, given it’s still supported.

	

The obvious response, noted by more than a few commenters, suggests using the Pixel 11 correctly. The NFC antenna is placed slightly higher than on other models, so the first suggestion appears to be “move your phone” to solve the Google Pixel’s NFC bug.

	

Of course, this would only apply if the Pixel 11’s NFC antenna were alone in experiencing this bug. Because it isn’t, it’s easier to point at a software update that made NFC unusable with Google Wallet. Some users note NFC still works in other functions, but not with payments.

Google has yet to respond, it seems. That doesn’t mean the company isn’t aware of the Pixel bug, but it might suggest users will need to wait a little longer for a fix. That being said, loss of tap-to-pay is a pretty big deal for a phone in 2026.

Are your NFC payments working?

title: Hollywood’s Newest Media Colossus: Paramount and Warner Bros. Merge Under Skydance
snippet: Skydance will now be one of the largest media companies in history, consolidating film studios, broadcast and cable networks, news and streaming.
fullText:
With Paramount CEO David Ellison overcoming the final hurdle blocking his expansion of the Paramount media empire, the billionaire media executive announced on X (formerly Twitter) that the newly merged entity combining Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery will be named Skydance.

The announcement comes after the company entered into a consent decree to settle antitrust claims brought by a group of 12 state attorneys general, who had sued in July over concerns that the merger would concentrate too much control over news networks, cable TV and the film industry. With the last legal opposition cleared, the path was open to finalize the massive the $111 billion merger on Sept. 21.

“Together, we are Skydance: a creative-first home for bold, quality storytelling,” Ellison posted on Friday. “We wanted a name that would give the combined company an identity of its own while allowing Paramount and Warner Bros. — and all our extraordinary brands — to remain in the spotlight.”

There was a year-long bidding battle for Warner Bros. Discovery, leaving Ellison as the top bidder after Netflix dropped out. The name Skydance comes from Ellison’s love of aviation and aerobatic “skydancing.” David’s father is Larry Ellison, who is co-founder and chief technology officer of Oracle and one of the richest people in the world.

What once was the peak, is now just the beginning.

Paramount and Warner Bros. shaped over a century of culture. By combining them, we aren't rewriting history — we're equipping these iconic studios with a more powerful engine. Together, we are Skydance: a creative-first home for… pic.twitter.com/uInLRY3IrE

— David Ellison (@davidellison) October 2, 2026

A Hollywood empire of studios, news, networks and streamers

As viewers, it’s unclear how streaming content from Warner Bros., HBO and Paramount via apps like HBO Max and Paramount Plus will change. But the merger will undeniably affect employees at the mega media company, now one of the largest in history. Much of the legal opposition concerned their fate, and the consent decree attempted to safeguard employment, film production and distribution and consumer pricing. 

In practice, employees usually lose out in corporate consolidation, regardless of protections. Harvard Business Review estimated that up to 30% of workers get laid off in mergers like these, where there’s a significant overlap in the business, though that oft-cited figure is from 2017. 

		

			

The bigger worry, though, is media monopoly. Critics worry that adding CNN to the company’s portfolio could lead to widespread restructuring and corporate upheaval, similar to recent struggles at the CBS News division. Corporate convergence also risks homogenizing news content by potentially suppressing divergent viewpoints — all for minimal reward, given that CBS’s own ratings are reportedly way down.

“If this trend of consolidation continues, we will be left searching dominant media outlets in vain for news and information that challenges the powerful and stands up for people who are struggling to pay monthly bills, put food on the table and engage in local civic life,” nonprofit watchdog Free Press co-CEO Jessica J. González said in a prepared statement earlier this week.

The Block the Merger coalition also posted a follow-up statement: “Allowing the Paramount Skydance-Warner Bros. Discovery merger to move forward with no meaningful structural remedies will cost jobs, mute creativity, weaken independent journalism, and damage our First Amendment rights. The ripples of this merger will be far-reaching, long-lasting, and impossible to contain.”

The Writers Guild of America East and Writers Guild of America West had filed a separate lawsuit to halt the merger, alleging that it was illegal and would harm writers. Once the state attorneys general backed out of the battle, WGA cited an inability to sustain legal costs on its own and dropped its companion lawsuit.

As part of the consent decree, Paramount agreed to establish an oversight board of journalists to protect the editorial independence of CNN and CBS News. Critics have called the oversight board “toothless,” noting that its members are appointed and paid by the company, that its authority is unclear and unbinding, and that final control rests with Ellison. 

We reached out to Skydance for comment and didn’t immediately hear back.

Disclosure: Lori Grunin has stock in Paramount from when CNET was owned by CBS.

snippet: Launched earlier this year, that useful little USB-C charger dongle for Google’s Pixel Watch 4 and Pixel Watch 5 smartwatches is currently discounted. more…
fullText:
Launched earlier this year, that useful little USB-C charger dongle for Google’s Pixel Watch 4 and Pixel Watch 5 smartwatches is currently discounted.

Google’s latest take on smartwatch charging debuted on last year’s Pixel Watch 4 series, with two pins popping out of the smartwatch to connect with a magnetic dock. Google’s official charging cable works well enough, but it’s just another thing to plug in when you’re traveling. 

Wasserstein, a long-time Made for Google accessory partner, launched a handy alternative earlier this year. A simple charger that attaches to the end of any USB-C cable give you the option to cut down on some bulk while still being able to easily top off your smartwatch on the go. Its price was in flux for quite a while, but eventually settled at $30.

Right now, though, it’s discounted to $25. Not a huge discount, but it certainly makes the handy charger an easier buy if you have any travel coming up through the end of the year.

	

Update 10/6: As a part of Amazon’s Prime Day sales holiday, Wasserstein has further discounted this to $19.99. You’ll need an Amazon Prime membership to take advantage of the deeper discount.

As a reminder, this works with all Pixel Watch 4 and Pixel Watch 5 smartwatches, regardless of if you’re using the 41mm or 45mm sizes. You’ll want to plug into at least 7.5W of power, but you’re likely getting that from whatever charger you’re using with your smartphone anyway. Just keep in mind that Pixel Watch 3 and prior cannot use this charger.

Trump Mobile appears to have suffered a data breach that may have exposed the data of 3,615 people, according to reports from PCMag and Straight Arrow News. The breach reportedly included names, home addresses, emails, phone numbers, and order information.

PCMag and Straight Arrow News contacted several individuals in the dataset, who confirmed that the leaked information was accurate. The leaked data may include people who never fully signed up for Trump Mobile, as one person told PCMag that they never managed to set up their account but still gave the company their email address and phone number. It also reportedly includes information related to Eric Brunnett, the chief information technology officer at The Trump Organization.

A hacking group called BYOD claimed responsibility for the potential breach. One member told PCMag that they breached the phone service by installing a remote access trojan on an employee of Liberty Mobile — the carrier that powers Trump Mobile’s network. The group also claims to have access to the backend of Trump Mobile’s website, according to Straight Arrow News.

The Verge reached out to Trump Mobile with a request for comment but didn’t immediately hear back.

title: Googlebook’s Android-integrated features won’t work with Samsung phones at launch
snippet: Googlebook is pitched as the laptop for Android users but, at launch, the vast majority of Android users can’t use the platform’s best features. more…
fullText:
Googlebook is pitched as the laptop for Android users but, at launch, the vast majority of Android users can’t use the platform’s best features.

Built on top of Android, Googlebook’s core pitch is to be the laptop for Android users, with deep integration between your smartphone and laptop. This includes a host of features such as instant hotspot, notification sync, phone file access, and the ability to continue tasks started on your phone from your Googlebook laptop. You can also stream apps from your phone’s display to your Googlebook directly.

In terms of deep integration, is a good pitch, but it won’t work for a lot of users at launch.

On a support page, Google confirms that Googlebook’s suite of Android integrations won’t work with any device running Android 16 or prior – Android 17 is the minimum requirement. 

	

Beyond that, Google also confirmed that Samsung devices are not supported at launch. Rather, support is rolling out “over the coming weeks.” It’s not mentioned whether Google or Samsung needs to push an update here, but it stands to reason that an update on Samsung’s end might be needed.

Support for Better Together features will be rolling out across all Android 17-supported Samsung devices over the coming weeks. Sorry for the inconvenience!

Meanwhile, Googlebook faces some other early hiccups, such as lacking support for Slack’s web app at launch, a key workplace app, as well as some apparent optimization issues for apps running on Intel hardware.

title: Facebook tests going Reels-first in India
snippet: Meta is testing a new Facebook UX in India that sends some users directly into full-screen video when they open the app, putting Reels front and center.
fullText:
Image Credits:Mateusz Slodkowski/SOPA Images/LightRocket / Getty Images	

	

						

5:38 AM PDT · October 6, 2026

											

			

Meta has started testing a new Facebook UX in India that sends some users directly into full-screen video when they open the app, putting Reels front and center.

First outlined in July by Facebook head Tom Alison, the test is designed to offer a more immersive, video-forward user experience. Alison said at the time that Meta planned to begin testing it later in the year in “video-heavy countries” outside the U.S., though he didn’t specify where. The company will explore bringing the user experience to the U.S. next year, he said.

Users included in the test can opt out and return to a Feed-first experience, Meta said. The classic feed will remain available as a second tab on the Facebook app.

The test comes as Meta moves to make video more central to Facebook. Last year, the company said all new videos posted to Facebook would be shared as Reels, regardless of their length or format, and it even renamed the app’s Video tab to “Reels.” Meta has previously said young adults spend about 60% of their time on Facebook watching videos.

India has long been a testing ground for Meta’s video efforts, particularly its push into short-form video. In 2020, Instagram began testing a dedicated Reels tab in the country, months after India banned TikTok. The company also tested a Reels-first experience for some Instagram users in India and South Korea last year that similarly sent them directly into the video UX when they opened the app.

The new test comes as video consumption rises across Meta’s apps in India. At least 97% of users surveyed in Meta-commissioned studies said they watch video on its platforms daily, and 89% of Gen Z respondents said they use Reels every day, per the figures the company released in June. Meta has described Reels as increasingly becoming India’s “personal and primary screen.”

India is Facebook’s largest market by users, with Meta’s advertising tools indicating an audience of more than 400 million people in the country.

title: Google Find Hub tags adding NFC support, better registration
snippet: According to the latest version of Google Play services, Find Hub tags are getting two new capabilities. more…
fullText:
According to the latest version of Google Play services, Find Hub tags are getting two new capabilities.

Version 26.39 of Google Play services has two Security & Privacy features related to the Find Hub network.

[Phone] With NFC support, you can quickly access Find Hub tag details and settings or identify lost tags when you tap the tag with your phone.

Find Hub devices that support NFC can be tapped with a phone to reveal “details and settings or identify lost tags.” At the moment, you have to place lost tags in an identification mode to get details, with the process varying between products. Tapping would be much easier.

NFC is not a common feature on Find Hub trackers. For example, it’s absent on the upcoming Pixel Tag. The Xiaomi Tag released earlier this year has NFC, but it appears limited to Apple’s Find My network. That said, Play services adding this support suggests such devices are coming.

	

[Phone] With the new registration flow, you can now set categories, rename tags, and configure features like Left-Behind Reminders when you first set up your Find Hub network tags, so you don’t have to configure them manually in the app later.

The second update introduces an improved setup process. It lets you set a category (Bag, Bike, Car, etc.), rename tags, and control other settings when you first register a device. Previously, you had to open the Find Hub app to do all this.

title: The Pixel 4 is still my favorite Google smartphone hardware, and it holds up
snippet: Google Pixel has evolved tremendously over the years, with some radically different designs showing up between generations. As the lineup turns 10, the Pixel 4 remains the one that stands out as my favorite smartphone hardware Google has made yet, and it’s not just about the looks. more…
fullText:
Google Pixel has evolved tremendously over the years, with some radically different designs showing up between generations. As the lineup turns 10, the Pixel 4 remains the one that stands out as my favorite smartphone hardware Google has made yet, and it’s not just about the looks.

Elephant in the room: The Pixel 4 series is objectively the worst pair of smartphones Google ever released. Funny, given that the beloved Pixel 4a came out of it, but it’s impossible to argue that Google nailed it here. Following up on its Pixel 3 series which, at the time, was the first launch that really started gainig traction, the Pixel 4 took a big swing in practically every way and it did not work.

But for all of its failings, the Pixel 4 remains my favorite piece of hardware overall.

Why?

	

I think this is the most unique smartphone Google made, and also the one most meant for actual people to use it. The looks themselves aren’t exactly groundbreaking. The mostly blank back with a single square camera module is relatively generic by today’s standards. I’ll still vouch for “Oh So Orange” any day – and still actively regret not keeping mine – but I’d also argue there’s beauty in the simplicity here. It’s timeless.

Of course, less timeless is that big forehead over the display. Used to house the Soli sensor and face unlock hardware, this was another place where Google made a big swing that didn’t work out. Fundamentally, I don’t think Google made a mistake here. The face unlock sensor still works, and even recognized me with a beard that I didn’t have 7 years ago when I was actively using this phone. Impressive! I still think I prefer Google’s forehead design to Apple’s iPhone notch of the time, but the cleverness of Apple’s Dynamic Island is way better than Google’s solution here. But with newer Pixels splitting the difference between security and hardware on face unlock, I think we’re in a pretty good spot nowadays. 

But what really lets the Pixel 4’s hardware live rent-free in my head is how it feels.

Again, for all of this phone’s failings, the physical hardware is truly just so nice. The soft-touch matte of the back panel hasn’t been replicated, and the visually contrasting side rails not only look great, but feel incredible in the hand. These really feel like they were born out of Google’s cozy, human take to product design of the time and I wish the company had continued down that path. 

Don’t get me wrong, the modern Pixel design is gorgeous. I’m a big fan of the camera bar and Google’s approach to color, but the aesthetic of the Pixel 4 is something that I wish we’d seen more of. It was such a great foundation that felt not just unique, but better at the time.

	

Of course, that was largely ruined by the shortcomings. Pixel 4’s legacy is largely around being too expensive, ditching a fingerprint sensor at exactly the wrong time, and truly atrocious battery life. 

Still, if I had any influence whatsoever over the next 10 years of Pixel design, stop number one would be revisiting some of the core design ideas behind the Pixel 4.

What do you think?

Google Pixel can use Tensor as long as it wants; it’s all the other specs I’m jealous of

title: OpenAI will start watermarking ChatGPT’s text in the EU
snippet: OpenAI will watermark ChatGPT and Codex text in the EU to comply with the AI Act. Editing can make the invisible marks harder to detect, it says.
fullText:
OpenAI will start adding an invisible watermark to text generated by ChatGPT and Codex in the European Union to comply with the EU AI Act, the company said Monday in a blog post.

The EU AI Act’s transparency rules, which took effect on August 2, require AI companies to mark AI-generated content in a way other systems can identify.

OpenAI said the watermark will roll out over the coming weeks to eligible ChatGPT and Codex users on all plans, but only in the EU. Developers using OpenAI’s API anywhere in the world can turn it on for select models starting today; it’s off by default. OpenAI said it is not making text watermarking a global default at launch.

The watermark is not an actual symbol, but works by subtly shaping the model’s word choices, leaving a pattern readers can’t see, but a detector can pick up. Because it lives in the words themselves, it travels with the text when it’s copied and pasted. OpenAI said the watermark doesn’t identify the user, and that it saw no meaningful change in its models’ performance with it switched on.

OpenAI also published a technical report for its method, called textGrain, alongside the announcement. Co-written with researchers from the University of Pennsylvania and Yale, it walks through an example of using a secret key to sort next-word predictions to finish the sentence. Add hundreds of these nudges together, and the detector can spot AI-generated content using only the text and the key.

Can the watermark be removed by editing? OpenAI’s tests suggest yes. In one test, replacing 10% of words with synonyms dropped detection from about 92% to 66%. The company also said short passages, math answers, and translated text are harder to detect.

Image Credits:OpenAI (opens in a new window)

“These limitations contribute to our decision to provide initial detector access only to approved researchers and expert organizations, who can help us evaluate reliability and responsible uses,” said the company.

OpenAI also cautioned that a missing watermark “does not prove human authorship.” The text could be too short or too heavily edited, or it could come from another company’s AI. 

“[Watermarks] can indicate that an OpenAI system generated or processed part of a passage, but not how much human judgment, editing, or creativity went into it,” the company said.

The announcement comes two months after Anthropic said it would watermark text generated by Claude, a move it’s applying worldwide. That decision drew backlash from some Claude users, who argued they had supplied “the instructions, context, decisions” while Claude was just “the tool.”

OpenAI had built a text watermark before but held off on releasing it, partly over concerns that users would switch to rivals that didn’t watermark, The Wall Street Journal reported in 2024.

Anthropic, Google, Meta, Microsoft, and OpenAI are among the companies that have committed to following the EU’s code of practice on AI-generated content.

title: Here’s how much Google is testing paying web publishers for AI Overview usage
snippet: A new report details how Google is testing paying web publishers for content used in its AI Overviews, including how much they’re making and how much that varies. more…
fullText:
A new report details how Google is testing paying web publishers for content used in its AI Overviews, including how much they’re making and how much that varies.

Google’s AI Overviews have drastically reshaped the web, and it’s hard to argue that it hasn’t harmed publishers across the web. Traffic is down almost universally, though Google insists AI isn’t to blame. Still, Google’s AI Overviews and other AI responses rely on publishers around the web to continue operating, something that’s increasingly difficult to do.

Following a report earlier this month, The Information is now offering a few more details on Google’s test to directly pay web publishers when their content is used in AI Overviews. 

The company is apparently paying around 100 digital publishers including “small to midsize blogs and websites.” Revenue seems to vary wildly, though. For some, it amounts to “less than one-tenth of 1% of their advertising revenue.” Some “smaller sites” have apparently earned less than $1,000 over several months, where another publisher that “joined a few months ago” has already made around $50,000-60,000 so far, “which doesn’t represent that much of its business.” Yet, another publisher said that a “bigger slice” was covered with Google’s payments earning “more than $1 million a year.”

	

The test, as previously reported, gives publishers insights into how often AI Overviews leverage their content. What’s not yet clear is how Google determines how much a publisher is paid, with some finding that “less widely covered” topics that “draw strong user interest” currently earn more, with examples including anime and gaming. 

It’s still unclear if Google plans to expand this program, but The Information reiterates that Google “needs these web publishers to stay active” for its models and answers to stay current and accurate.
