title: Google announces Gemini 4 Argon as its new frontier model
snippet: Gemini 4 Argon is Google’s “next era of frontier intelligence” and built for “deep reasoning across complex, long-horizon workflows.” It follows the cancellation of Gemini 3.5 Pro and focus on 3.8 Flash. more…
fullText:
Gemini 4 Argon is Google’s “next era of frontier intelligence” and built for “deep reasoning across complex, long-horizon workflows.” It follows the cancellation of Gemini 3.5 Pro and focus on 3.8 Flash.

With this new model (which has a new naming scheme), Google wants to offer “frontier-level capabilities” across coding, knowledge work, cybersecurity defense, and creative writing.

Gemini 4 Argon’s output token limit is 1M tokens (up from 64K) to allow for longer and more complex use cases. This is paired with expanded coding, reasoning, and multimodal capabilities.

When the model has the headroom to think deeply and generate hundreds of thousands of tokens in a single trajectory, it adds a new level of depth in reasoning to solve tough problems in one go.

In terms of benchmarks, Google touts a DeepSWE v1.1 score of 77.9%. Claude Opus 5.5 comes in at 74.2% followed by GPT-6 Astra’s 74.1%.

	

Google trained Gemini 4 Argon to be “highly capable at cybersecurity defense” with leaps over 3.8 Flash Cyber. The model will be made available “without cyber guardrails” to trusted defenders and internal Google teams so that they can “leverage its full frontier-level cybersecurity defense capabilities.”

“On CWE-bench v1, which evaluates the model’s ability to remediate security vulnerabilities, Argon ties for first place with a top score of 68%”

Outside of coding, Gemini 4 Argon also has “leading performance across other domain specific evaluations,” such as Vals Finance Agent v2 (multi-step financial research) and Harvey’s Legal Agent Benchmark (legal research and drafting).

“On AutomationBench, Zapier’s benchmark measuring end-to-end execution across core business functions, Argon ranks #1 with a score of 51.3%.”

“…on LVBench, which measures long video understanding, Argon is state of the art with a score of 91.7%.”

Gemini 4 Argon is “rolling out soon,” starting with Google AI Ultra subscribers and paid API customers. 

“Argon will launch at an introductory price of $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens, with cached input tokens priced at 95% off input token price.”

“After the introductory period expires, the price of $4 per 1M input tokens and $20 per 1M output tokens will apply.”

So far, it has been made available to trusted testers and cyber defenders (via Fairwind Program). Before the broader release, Google is focusing on:

Defending against misuse from cyber or chemical, biological, radiological, and nuclear (CBRN) attacks: Google has improved “techniques to monitor the model’s internal activations to spot misuse.”

Defending against prompt injection attacks: Google’s “most resilient model yet against indirect prompt injections” with “leading in prompt injection robustness on the Gray Swan’s Indirect Prompt Injection (IPI) Benchmark.”

Hardening systems: “we are hardening our sandboxed environments by isolating and sealing them before high-risk training or evaluations begin.”

Monitoring for misalignment: Google is “deploying misalignment mitigations that monitor Argon’s chain-of-thought and actions and stop execution when necessary.”

“We used a similar system to monitor our training runs and send alerts to a dedicated incident response team, taking careful precautions against feeding the findings back into training so as to not risk shaping Argon’s reasoning to evade our monitoring.”

Inside Google, Gemini 4 Argon is already powering internal workflows with “thousands of Googlers highlighting the model’s strengths in specialized coding tasks, conducting deeper research, and writing quality.” The company shared some examples today:

Memory efficiency: A team of Argon agents analyzed fleet-wide profiling telemetry to autonomously identify and apply memory optimizations across Google’s data centers, freeing up over 300 TiB of memory once rolled out, with an estimated 500 TiB to 1 PiB in total savings.

Large Scale Codebase Migrations and Optimizations: Argon agents are working on migrating C/C++ codebases to Rust across Google—scaling from tens of thousands of lines in core libraries like re2, libgav1 up to 800K+ lines for the Fuchsia OS Zircon kernel. Given the criticality of many of these systems, such large-scale rewrites are undergoing rigorous automated and manual auditing, emulation testing, and review before rolling out to production.

For libgav1, Google’s open source software for decoding video, Argon agents took an existing Rust port and replaced 32K lines of SIMD code by running many rounds of profile-guided experiments, studying the compiler’s output, producing safe Rust so the compiler would vectorize it automatically. The end result is a memory-safe video decoder that runs 2.7x faster than the Rust port, with identical video output, bringing it closer to the optimized C++.

title: I Got a First Look at Vitamix’s First Juicer, and I’m in Love
snippet: The MaxExtract has turned me into a juice enthusiast.
fullText:
When a company enters a new product category, I’m always skeptical. As a Vitamix fan, a brand known for its blenders, I had reservations when I heard it was releasing its first cold-press juicer. Yet, I got a first look at the product and can safely say that this juicer lives up to the Vitamix name. 

Announced on Monday and available for purchase on Oct. 15, the MaxExtract Cold Press Juicer uses slow-masticating technology to extract juice from fruits, veggies and leafy greens. 

The MaxExtract is easy to operate

Assembling the juicer took less time and effort than I expected. Then, all you have to do is chop your produce into 2-inch pieces, throw them into the juicer’s 5.3-inch hopper (which can hold a surprising amount of ingredients) and let the MaxExtract handle the rest in minutes. 

			

More from CNET

The light-up front dial makes it extra simple. Turn it to the on position to start the juicing process, to the off position when it’s done and reverse it when there’s a clog. However, I haven’t experienced a clog after making several batches of juice. 

The dial has a light behind it. A nice touch.Anna Gragert/CNET

It comes with everything you need

The MaxExtract includes a pusher to push ingredients down, a cleaning brush, pulp and juice containers and two strainers: a fine-mesh for less pulp and smoother juice and an easy-clean for more pulp but an easier clean, as the name suggests. 

I especially appreciate that the juice container includes measurements on the side. 

The juice container also has a handle, making it easier to pour the liquid into a glass. Anna Gragert/CNET

All detachable parts are dishwasher-safe

I love that all the detachable components are dishwasher-safe on both the top and bottom racks. The pulp outlet can also be opened to make removing pulp and cleaning even simpler.

As someone who has never used a juicer, I have to say that the MaxExtract has converted me. It creates a smooth, fresh-tasting juice and takes any effort out of the process, including cleanup. 

One of the most satisfying parts is watching the pulp emerge.Anna Gragert/CNET

Size is to be expected

The user manual lists the MaxExtract as 17.7 by 8.5 by 7.7 inches and 8.14 pounds. However, you can remove the hopper and chamber from the base if the full unit is too tall for your cabinets. 

By comparison, the MaxExtract is narrower and shallower than the $599 Nama J2 Cold Press Juicer, which measures 17.7 by 9.8 by 9 inches and weighs 12.1 pounds. CNET’s best budget juicer, the 11.14-pound Hamilton Beach Easy Clean, is shorter but wider and deeper, measuring 15.31 by 13 by 9 inches.

Before purchasing any juicer, make sure it will fit in your space.Anna Gragert/CNET

Vitamix MaxExtract availability and price 

Available in black or white with a glass front on Oct. 15, the MaxExtract will be $500. You can buy it on Vitamix.com or Amazon and it comes with a five-year limited warranty.

fullText:
New Apple products are reportedly launching on October 13, including an updated Apple TV 4K. Here are the two major upgrades rumored for the new Apple TV.

When Siri AI was first unveiled by Apple this June, the company presented it as a cross-platform revamp that would work the same regardless of the device you’re using.

The new Siri debuted on iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple Watch, and Vision Pro. But curiously, there’s never been mention made of Siri AI on Apple TV or HomePod. And out of all the OS 27 updates that shipped last month, tvOS and HomePod software are the only ones missing the new Siri.

The Apple TV 4K hasn’t been updated since 2022, and that model has an A15 chip that debuted in 2021.

But rumors indicate the new Apple TV 4K being unveiled next week will bring a big chip upgrade, boasting an A19 or A19 Pro chip.

	

Leaker Aaron Perris discovered a reference to the new hardware model in Apple code with an ‘AppleTV18,1’ identifier. This ‘18,1’ numbering scheme was also used for the iPhone 17 line, thus pointing to an A19-class chip being used.

I suspect it will be an A19 Pro rather than A19, since the latter doesn’t support the ability to customize Siri AI’s voice pace and expressivity. With Siri AI being a major focal point of the new Apple TV, the A19 Pro seems a safer bet.

title: Google Docs and Drive now support markdown files natively
snippet: Spurred by the use of markdown files in the AI age, Google Drive and Google Docs are adding full, native support for markdown (.md) files. more…
fullText:
Spurred by the use of markdown files in the AI age, Google Drive and Google Docs are adding full, native support for markdown (.md) files.

Google has been building out markdown support in Drive for years now, but prior steps largely included converting markdown into a format that Docs could use.

Now, Google Drive and its suite of apps can open, edit, and fully use markdown files throughout Docs and other apps. This includes real-time editing and comments with full rendering of the formatting of markdown documents. Google also points out that this benefits AI use cases such as having AI agents collaborate on documents and even syncing with Gemini Notebook.

Google explains:

	

Now that users can handle markdown files natively in Google Docs, they can open, edit, and collaborate on markdown files without changing the file type. Editing Markdown files in Docs also enables both users and agents to collaborate without forcing anyone to write raw syntax, handle manual file conversions, or give up Docs’ real-time editing and commenting tools.

Drive also now supports rendered markdown, so you can view fully formatted, beautiful documents with clickable links and structured tables right in Drive.

Google’s Chandu Thota calls out that markdown “has become the common language between humans and AI agents.”

Markdown support in Google Drive and Docs is rolling out starting today but may take up to 15 days to show up for everyone. It’s enabled by default, even on admin-controlled accounts.

fullText:
Andrew Liszewski

 

is a senior reporter who’s been covering and reviewing the latest gadgets and tech since 2006, but has loved all things electronic since he was a kid.

Following more images of the previously leaked Google Fitbit Edge surfacing a few days ago, new details about the upcoming fitness tracker have been revealed, including potential features and pricing. The Fitbit Edge will reportedly sell for €179 in Europe, and £159 in the UK, according to leaked details shared by Dealabs. Given the €99/£85 pricing of the $99 screen-free Fitbit Air in those regions, 9to5Google estimates the new Fitbit Edge will cost around $180 in the US.

The Fitbit Edge will feature a 1.34-inch always-on OLED touchscreen and will run Fitbit OS with access to Google Play. It will connect to Android and iOS devices over Bluetooth and in addition to GPS it will include a variety of sensors including an accelerometer, a barometer, an altimeter, and a gyroscope plus multiple optical sensors for measuring heart rate and blood oxygen saturation (SpO2) and electrical sensors for capturing ECGs.

The Edge’s fitness monitoring capabilities will include tracking steps, distance, calories, skin temperature, sleep, cardiac load, and menstrual cycles. It will also track physical activities like running, swimming, golf, and over 40 different exercises with real-time coaching and personalized fitness programs provided by Google Gemini. The fitness tracker will also watch for the telltale signs of serious medical conditions like atrial fibrillation and irregular heart rhythms with alerts when they’re detected.

A user-replaceable lithium-ion battery is rated for up to seven days of battery life but that will be reduced to up to two days with its screen always on. The Fitbit Edge will also feature an IP68 water resistance rating and is expected to launch in four color options like the Pixel Watch 5 including obsidian and matte black, olive and satin pyrite, canyon and champagne gold, and fog and polished silver.

Everyone has issues with iPhone storage. Even if you use iCloud, Apple has a large gap between tiers, with it immediately jumping from 200GB at $3 to 2TB at $10. If you just want a little bit more than 200GB, it can be hard to justify that upgrade. HEVCut aims to fix this by optimizing your photo library, without needing to delete anything.

Highlights

To be clear, HEVCut also offers the normal features you’d expect in a photo cleanup app: it helps you find duplicate shots, as well as the ability to easily delete photos in a nice swipe left/right interface.

That’s not the key highlight, though. As I said earlier, it can go through your photos library and compress media. It’s highly effective, so you save 50-80% on each file, while not losing much in image quality.

It runs all on device, so you’re not giving up your privacy to compress your images. This can easily help you save hundreds of gigs of local or iCloud storage.

It also supports a nifty video editor for trimming down videos to shorter lengths to share with friends, in case you tend to record entire events when you only need a few key moments.

HEVCut is available for free on the App Store in a limited capacity, but to unlock the full experience, including the best resolution settings, you’ll need HEVCut Pro for $24.99/year or $39.99 for the lifetime upgrade. There’s a $0.49 1 week trial if you’d like to give it a shot before committing.

title: This tool frees up Apple Intelligence storage on macOS, but think twice before using it
snippet: A new open-source tool is going viral over its promise to let users who aren’t interested in Apple Intelligence reclaim 12GB or more of storage on their Macs. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
A new open-source tool is going viral over its promise to let users who aren’t interested in Apple Intelligence reclaim 12GB or more of storage on their Macs. Here are the details.

’Turn off Apple Intelligence on macOS 27 and remove its downloaded models’

Like many companies adding AI tools and models across their platforms, Apple has faced criticism for features that take up storage space some users consider unnecessary.

While Apple Intelligence required up to 7GB of storage on macOS 26, that figure has increased significantly on macOS 27, with Apple now saying its latest models can require up to 14GB on newer Macs.

In response to this, indie developer Om Lahore published a project called RemoveMacAI on GitHub late last week, which promises to “turn off Apple Intelligence on macOS 27 and remove its downloaded models.”

As Lahore explains, his tool enables a configuration profile that applies Apple’s own restriction keys to turn off Apple Intelligence features, while also using the company’s asset service to remove downloaded models and prevent macOS from downloading them again.

He also explains exactly what the tool removes, which features it disables, and what users can expect after running it:

Features turned off: Siri (including “Hey Siri” and the menu bar icon), Writing Tools, Genmoji, Image Playground, the ChatGPT extension, summaries in Mail, Messages, Safari, Notes and notifications, Mail smart replies, inline text predictions, Spatial Photos, Photos Clean Up and Xcode predictive code completion.

Models removed: the Apple Intelligence foundation models and the models for image generation and Genmoji, Spatial Photos, Photos Clean Up and Xcode code completion.

And

What stops working? The features listed above, apps that use Apple’s on-device models (the Foundation Models framework and the Use Model action in Shortcuts), Visual Intelligence and natural-language editing in Calendar.

Lahore notes that dictation still works after running RemoveMacAI, as it “is a separate setting, and its speech models are not removed.”

Finally, he adds that the entire process can be reversed, with full details and instructions available here.

9to5Mac’s take

While part of the outcry over how much storage Apple Intelligence takes up on the Mac appears to be the same knee-jerk reaction against anything AI-related, there is a legitimate argument to be made for users with limited internal storage, particularly on 256GB Macs, where reclaiming 12GB or more can make a meaningful difference.

There is also a broader question of basic control over one’s own operating system, as users who have no interest in Apple Intelligence should arguably have a straightforward way to turn it off completely and recover the storage its models occupy, just as they can with other apps and certain optional parts of the system.

That said, there is no telling whether Apple will attempt to get the project removed from GitHub, or change the underlying mechanisms in macOS to make Apple Intelligence models harder to remove.

Likewise, there is no way to know how disabling or removing these components could affect macOS itself going forward, or even third-party apps that increasingly rely on Apple’s models to provide basic functionality.

While RemoveMacAI is open source and does not require disabling System Integrity Protection, it still relies on configuration profiles, restriction keys, and system services that Apple could change at any time.

	

That means a future macOS update could render parts of the tool ineffective, or potentially leave users dealing with unexpected behavior until the project is updated.

For now, anyone considering RemoveMacAI should understand that this is an unofficial third-party tool making system-level changes, and should be comfortable with the way it works.

To be completely clear, RemoveMacAI seems like a well-intentioned open-source project aimed at giving Mac users more autonomy and control over what runs on their computers and how their storage is used. It’s just impossible to know whether Apple will view it the same way.

title: Android Auto might start requiring Android 11 or later soon, driver reports suggest
snippet: If you’re still holding onto an older Android phone as your daily driver, it might be losing its ability to get you where you need to be. Some users are starting to see notifications warning that their device will no longer be supported through Android Auto, suggesting the days of Android 10 are coming to a close. more…
fullText:
If you’re still holding onto an older Android phone as your daily driver, it might be losing its ability to get you where you need to be. Some users are starting to see notifications warning that their device will no longer be supported through Android Auto, suggesting the days of Android 10 are coming to a close.

Currently, Android Auto’s OS requirement is split into two tracks: wireless Auto support requires Android 11, while wired support requires just Android 9 Pie. A series of user reports over the weekend on Reddit (via Android Authority) suggest Google might be looking to unify those standards. The notification being delivered to drivers — most of whom appear to be running Android 10, not Android 9 Pie — simply states that Android Auto will “soon stop working on this phone,” without any additional context. Google has yet to update its current support page for Auto’s base-level requirements, but it’s not too difficult to read between the lines here.

Typically, I don’t think most users would see this change as a big surprise, even if cutting off support for certain phones always comes with controversy. In this case, though, it’s about as bad a time as you could pick for Google to be increasing device requirements. Some of the phones cited in these Reddit reports include Samsung’s Galaxy Note 9, Galaxy S9, and Xperia XZ2 Compact — all three of which offer experiences I’d argue are no longer available on the vast majority of modern Android devices. Add in the ever-increasing price of smartphones both new and not-so-new, and it feels a bit like a kick in the teeth to some drivers, no matter how old their hardware currently is.

If you’re an affected Android 9 Pie or Android 10 user and you need Android Auto support for your car, I would suggest starting to shop around for a replacement device running at least Android 11. While it’s a bad time to be in the market for any new gadget, there’s no obvious end to price hikes on the horizon, and picking up a phone now can save you some cash in the long run. We’ve reached out to Google for clarification on its Auto OS requirement plans and whether or not there’s a timeline for affected drivers to upgrade, and will update when we hear back.

title: After Factory’s public spat with Khosla, Menlo proudly invests
snippet: Days after Vinod Khosla called Factory a struggling also-ran, Menlo has shown up with a check and a glowing blog post.
fullText:
Menlo Ventures partner Matt Murphy and his team announced Monday in a blog post that the firm has invested in AI coding startup Factory.

Menlo declined to comment on how much it invested but said the deal was part of Factory’s latest funding round announced last month at a $5 billion valuation. A source familiar with the deal told us the investment was significant to Menlo — not a token gesture — and that Menlo would have invested more had there been room on the cap table.

Ordinarily, something like this wouldn’t necessarily be news; startups often extend previous rounds to add new investors. But last week, Factory co-founder and CEO Matan Grinberg was embroiled in a very public airing of dirty laundry when he alleged that he had fired investor Chris Degnan of firm RPT Partners from his role as board advisor. Grinberg said he feared Degnan may have shared confidential information with Factory’s biggest competitor, Cognition. The accusation followed Degnan’s move to Cognition as its chief revenue officer.

A who’s who of the tech industry came out of the woodwork either to support Degnan and condemn Factory, or vice versa, but none was more surprising than Vinod Khosla. Khosla’s firm is an investor in both Factory and Cognition. But that didn’t stop the venerable VC from calling Factory a desperate “struggling second tier competitor,” and accusing Grinberg of lying about firing Degnan and impugning his character. Degnan disputed Grinberg’s story, saying he resigned and that he’d rebuffed a competing job offer from Grinberg.

So Menlo’s full-throated endorsement of Factory, which praised its founders, its tech, and its relationship with its customers, is more than a feather in Factory’s cap. It’s a statement that Factory is not in the state that Khosla implied it was.

Murphy famously bet his firm on Anthropic back when it appeared to be an also-ran to OpenAI and has been on a hot streak ever since, landing deals with Lovable and Legora, for instance. So now some VCs are calling Factory “the next Anthropic.“

Sequoia’s Shaun Maguire, also a Factory backer who came out on X in support of Grinberg last week, appears thrilled with Menlo’s endorsement, saying the firm is “on a tear.” Notably, Menlo is not an investor in competitor Cognition.

title: Vinod Khosla believes ex-Deepmind engineer’s Wajo will win agent market on trust
snippet: Wajo's Fo agent can hire humans to complete a task.
fullText:
The personal-agent space has become closely competitive in the recent weeks, with Meta’s Muse, OpenAI’s Dot, and Instinct taking the lead and more competitors being launched each week. But Vinod Khosla is betting on former Google and DeepMind engineer Shivani Poddar’s Wajo for one simple reason: trust.

“I think the most important thing in an agent, because it’s acting for you, is trust. You have to have trust in the agent, and I think compared to either Muse or Instinct, Wajo is the most trustworthy because it is architected to focus on trust and safety first, and some of the others are not,” Khosla told TechCrunch over a call.

“I mean, who wants to give all their data to Facebook [Meta]? I don’t. And if I give my data to Facebook, I’m the product, not the product I am buying, because they are in the ad business. So trust is important, and most people don’t trust a large company like Facebook,” he added.

In broad strokes, Wajo’s Fo agent works very much like Muse or Instinct. The agent can work across iMessage and WhatsApp, and has a web interface with cards of potential tasks. Errands are organized into categories like “scheduling,” “gifting,” and “life admin.” Its agent can also call businesses or other people on your behalf, booking or cancelling services as needed.

In a few early tests, I asked it to call an airline to check for upgrades, and it successfully did so. However, when I asked it to call my partner and remind her to feed the cats, the call didn’t go smoothly, and disclosures were less clear. As rivals like Instinct and Muse are also rolling out calling ability slowly, we might see more discussions around how an AI calling on someone’s behalf should disclose itself. One of the unique things about the tool is that it can hire a human to complete a task when needed.

Apart from this, Fo can create a virtual credit card and pay on your behalf without disclosing your details. The agent also has its own email and can converse with people and businesses. When websites or services block AI agents, Fo can inform the user to take action or create a group with the user and the business for verification.

The startup has also secured backing from Jeff Dean and Gokul Rajaram apart, but didn’t specify the money raised. Wajo didn’t provide any numbers around users but said that its being used in 107 countries and has grown 10x since its launch in late September.

Founder story

Prior to founding Wajo, Poddar worked in various engineering roles at Meta, Google, and DeepMind and was invovled in making the first Facebook assistant. She said that she wanted to build products that were useful to people. 

“The whole journey of bringing Gemini to the world and building safety for it made me realize the technological depth that you need to do this. Google is so good in technology that sometimes it can be left behind in product. I thought I needed to do something that is both technology and product at the same time. It has to be something different, which is very grounded in what the user needs,” Poddar told TechCrunch over a call.

Image Credits: WajoImage Credits:Wajo

Former Google engineering lead mirrored Khosla’s thoughts around Trust, and emphasized that it was one of the core principles for Wajo.

“Trust is something you have to build from the get-go because one of the technological things that has not been solved yet is teaching agents to unlearn. If they get access to your personal data on day zero, they will always have it for the future. I think trust needs to be built from day zero, not only in your architecture, but in product choices,” she said.

The company is doing work in a few areas in relation to trust and safety. It has applied for a patent for its virtual card system that hides users’ information from sites. For calls, the company said it will include a “trusted contact” list for users whose agents can call them. When you get a call, you can also tell the agent not to call you again, and Wajo records that preference. 

The startup’s challenge is not to raise privacy concerns like other agents, especially as it is marketing safety as a core value. It also claims that despite tools like Muse being blocked by Amazon, its architecture follows the ecommerce service’s terms of service. 

Wajo said that in the coming months it will explore how its Fo agent will work in social settings across multiple users, with the core idea of keeping privacy intact.

title: Bluesky wants to give you your own domain on the open web
snippet: Bluesky says the process will still take 18-24 months, so don't expect your new, shortened 'bsky' handle any time soon.
fullText:
Bluesky CEO Toni Schneider teased long-term plans on Monday when he shared that the company has applied to make “.bsky” an internet domain suffix, like .com or .org. If approved, users will be able to turn their longer social handles into shorter, cleaner domain names.

For instance, instead of @sarahp.bsky.social, my handle could one day become just “sarahp.bsky.”

That could leave Bluesky room to innovate around user profiles, turning them from a simple page that houses someone’s bio and their posts into a more comprehensive personal home page that establishes someone’s online presence.

Bluesky’s application hasn’t been approved yet. Schneider said that ICANN (Internet Corporation for Assigned Names and Numbers), the nonprofit that oversees domain names for the internet, will publish the applications for the new domains on October 7, 2026, and Bluesky’s request will be among them. It’ll take 18 to 24 months for the process to be completed.

Reached for comment, Bluesky said it hasn’t finalized how .bsky domains would be requested, registered or distributed, but the company did say it had no plans to either sell or monetize the domains.

That’s a notable decision given that domain registration can be a profitable business that could serve as a potential revenue stream for a startup that has raised significant funds but isn’t (yet?) generating ad revenue.

However, Bluesky says selling domains goes against its belief in an open web.

“Domains are a big part of the open web, as they allow users to control their own online identity,” said Rose Wang, Bluesky’s COO, in a comment shared with TechCrunch. “Bluesky was built on the belief that you should own your presence online, not rent it from a platform that can take it away.”

by  Emma Roth

Oct 6, 2026, 1:32 PM UTC

Image: The Verge

Emma Roth

 

is a news writer who covers the streaming wars, consumer tech, crypto, social media, and much more. Previously, she was a writer and editor at MUO.

Paramount has completed its $110 billion acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery, forming a combined company known as Skydance. The merger officially puts Paramount and WBD’s film studios, along with major networks and brands like HBO, CBS News, and CNN, under one roof.

The road to the media megamerger has been a rocky one for Paramount, which secured an agreement in February after waging a months-long battle against Netflix for WBD. Since then, it has faced criticism from both lawmakers and Hollywood talent about the negative impact of media consolidation.

Paramount cleared its last major hurdle last month, as it settled with 12 states that sued to block the deal over antitrust concerns. Under the settlement, Skydance must release a minimum number of theatrical films over the next five years, starting with 30 in years one and two. It must also spend at least $300 million more on production in the US compared to what the companies spent last year combined.

David Ellison will lead Skydance alongside Ynon Kreiz, the former chairman and CEO of Mattel.

“Today is a historic day, not just for Skydance but for our entire industry,” Ellison said in the announcement. “From the start, our ambition was to bring these two storied studios together and create a stronger competitor, with the talent, resources, and reach to tell great stories in every genre, on every platform, for audiences everywhere. Now that ambition is a reality.”

title: Lucid Motors’ EV output falls to lowest level in almost 2 years
snippet: The company is deliberately limiting production after years of struggling to find mass-market demand for its EVs.
fullText:
Lucid Motors built 2,954 electric vehicles (EVs) in the third quarter of this year, a 54% drop from a year ago, as the company purposely limits production to better meet demand for its EVs.

This was the third straight quarter in which the number of EVs Lucid built has declined. It’s also the lowest quarterly output since the first quarter of 2025, which was just after Lucid Motors started production of its second EV, the Gravity SUV.

Lucid delivered 3,806 EVs in the third quarter, roughly flat with the second quarter and down about 200 vehicles from the third quarter of 2025. The company has struggled to find buyers for either of its first two luxury EVs. In five of the last six quarters, it built more vehicles than it delivered.

Lucid’s new CEO, Silvio Napoli, has spent the last few months leading an effort to “simplify the company.” That effort has included laying off around 1,500 employees, streamlining the company’s leadership, and eliminating a second shift at its factory in Arizona in a bid to reach cost savings of $1.4 billion. Lucid also delayed the release of its third EV, the Cosmos. That model is supposed to be much cheaper, starting at under $50,000.

The third-quarter figures, released Monday afternoon, come just a few days after rival EV upstart Rivian posted its best quarter in history on the back of the R2, its new, more affordable SUV. Although Rivian didn’t break out specific delivery figures for the R2, the company shipped nearly 20,000 vehicles in the third quarter, the first full quarter with the R2 in production, up from 12,194 in the second quarter.

Lucid’s failure to find a large market of buyers for its EVs is even more stark when compared with the promises the company made when it went public in 2021. That year, Lucid Motors merged with a special purpose acquisition company and estimated it would ship as many as 90,000 EVs in 2024 alone. The company raised $4 billion in the transaction.

On Lucid’s second-quarter earnings call in August, Napoli spoke about why he thinks the company has failed to make a dent in the EV market.

“While there is no question that Lucid brought leading innovations and outstanding products to the market, we have disappointed on several fronts, and for far too long,” he said. “We have not executed consistently. We missed commitments, launched products before they were ready, underinvested in service, responded too slowly to quality issues, and allowed complexity to slow decisions down.”

The Cosmos’ lower price could, in theory, let Lucid access a wider market, but Napoli cautioned shareholders that rushing the new EV out could create more trouble.

“We will not repeat the mistakes of the past by bringing a product to market before it is ready,” Napoli said on the call.

title: YouTube says Shorts recommendations won’t surface unoriginal content
snippet: YouTube says it wants to ‘focus on originality’ in a push to surface better Shorts recommendations for users. more…
fullText:
YouTube says it wants to ‘focus on originality’ in a push to surface better Shorts recommendations for users.

Shorts is built on quick and attention-grabbing content, which makes cutting portions of long-form videos one of the easiest ways to put out quick videos with high view potential. Of course, that also means channels can just as easily take content from other established creators and stamp out short-form videos from it.

YouTube says it’s adjusted its Shorts recommendations so users will see less unoriginal content. Users who upload content that blatantly steals video from another channel will not get the same reach as they did before the change, according to what YouTube laid out in its release.

To improve the Shorts experience for everyone, we’re updating our recommendation systems to further prioritize original content and reduce the reach of content re-uploaded from other creators without adding anything of your own.

There’s a small amount of room for interpretation. YouTube’s language seems to imply that Shorts that contain no changes form another’s work would be affected, but no clear line in the sand has been drawn out.

	

Remember, YouTube announced it was testing a new feature that would let users reimagine other channels’ videos using AI, which was released in March. Whether those videos will still be surfaced in the recommendations system is unclear.

The change should mean users will see a focus on original content, and creators that upload original Shorts will likely be rewarded. YouTube hasn’t detailed a rollout date for this change, but it sounds like it may be live already.

title: iOS 27 breaks 15 years of muscle memory on iPhone and iPad
snippet: Since iOS 5 in 2011, the iPhone and iPad have included Notification Center, a central place to find alerts from various apps in chronological order. Starting with iOS 27, Apple is making a major change to how users open Notification Center on iPhone and iPad. iOS 27 is here after a summer of beta releases. The behavior changed slightly between the first two releases. However, this change shipped, and I’m still adjusting to it. more…
fullText:
Since iOS 5 in 2011, the iPhone and iPad have included Notification Center, a central place to find alerts from various apps in chronological order.

Starting with iOS 27, Apple is making a major change to how users open Notification Center on iPhone and iPad.

iOS 27 is here after a summer of beta releases. The behavior changed slightly between the first two releases. However, this change shipped, and I’m still adjusting to it.

Siri AI takes over the swipe gesture for a lot of the iPhone and iPad top edge

Opening Notification Center is unchanged on iOS 27 and iPadOS 27 by default. However, enabling Siri AI changes a key swipe gesture on both iPhone and iPad.

One of the many ways of invoking Siri AI, once enabled, is by swiping down from the center of the top edge of your iPhone or iPad display. This previously opened Notification Center.

You can still access Notification Center by swiping down from the top-left corner once Siri AI is enabled. Alerts now animate in from the top left corner. This is a way to point users toward Notification Center’s smaller surface area.

Apple is greatly prioritizing Siri AI access in iOS 27. The majority of the top edge is devoted to invoking the new Siri experience.

The last time Apple made a change to accessing Notification Center came when Control Center moved from a swipe up gesture from the bottom to a top-right corner swipe down gesture on iPhone X. Apple later unified this experience across devices.

Notifications now live in the top left corner

Now it’s Notification Center’s turn to be put in the corner. On iPadOS 27 beta 1 in particular, the area above Home screen app icons was pretty much devoted to invoking Siri AI. The area for opening Notification Center actually shrank if you disable displaying AM/PM or the date.

	

Apple improved this with iPadOS 27 beta 2, creating a more uniform region on either side. It’s roughly the size of two app columns with Notification Center on the left and Control Center on the right. The rest is for invoking Siri. 

After 15 years of muscle memory, it’ll take some time to determine if this change is worth it or something that should be reconsidered. In the meantime, early feedback sounds overwhelmingly positive around Apple’s new Siri AI system. Hearing that Siri is good now will also take some getting used to, I’m sure.

After months of using the new behavior, I’m certain I’d toggle it off if there were a setting to do so. Since there’s no option to disable invoking Siri from the top middle swipe down, the only thing to do is build new muscle memory around avoiding the center.

What do you think? Would you change this back if you could? Is accessing Siri from the swipe-down gesture worth the change? Share your thoughts in the comments.

title: This fake Mac Zoom installer has a sneaky way to bypass Gatekeeper
snippet: Cybersecurity company Jamf has discovered a fake Mac installer for the videoconferencing app Zoom that uses a sneaky way to bypass Apple’s Gatekeeper protection against malware. The malware does actually install Zoom, but also an infostealer that captures data and sends it to the attacker’s server … more…
fullText:
Cybersecurity company Jamf has discovered a fake Mac installer for the videoconferencing app Zoom that uses a sneaky way to bypass Apple’s Gatekeeper protection against malware.

The malware does actually install Zoom, but also an infostealer that captures data and sends it to the attacker’s server …

Normally, when you try to install a Mac app that Apple hasn’t notarized, macOS will refuse to open it. There is a workaround to allow you to do so, but it’s somewhat fiddly, and attackers have to find some way to persuade users to do it.

The criminals behind the malware Jamf has dubbed CloudSyncD have found a clever way to make this seem more normal to users. The app installer dropper includes a background image with instructions, as shown above.

CloudSyncD arrives as a disk image that mounts as a volume named Zoom, laid out to look like any ordinary Mac installer: an application icon on the left, an alias to Applications on the right. The difference is the background image, which carries a numbered Setup list telling the victim to open System Settings, go to Privacy & Security, scroll to the Security section, click Open Anyway, and enter their administrator password. Those are instructions to bypass Gatekeeper.

You kind of have to admire the creativity of this.

Once the malware is installed, it can record user-entered data and send it to the attackers as frequently as every eight seconds.

As always, you should only ever install Mac apps from the official Mac App Store or the websites of developers you trust.

title: Apple’s new ‘homeOS’ will launch this month, here’s what’s coming
snippet: Apple reportedly plans to launch new Home products on October 13 alongside an all-new operating system rumored to be called ‘homeOS.’ Here are the details. more…
fullText:
Apple reportedly plans to launch new Home products on October 13 alongside an all-new operating system rumored to be called ‘homeOS.’ Here are the details.

homeOS will run on new ‘HomePad’ product, featuring mix of other Apple OS designs

Apple’s highly anticipated ‘HomePad’ smart home hub is reportedly being unveiled on October 13. And per Mark Gurman, it will run on a brand new operating system that’s rumored to be called ‘homeOS.’

A recent Bloomberg report offers a lot of details on what to expect from homeOS. It reportedly features a blend of other Apple OS designs, including:

iPhone-style widgets

iPad-like app designs

Apple Watch-style icons for its Home Screen 

The default UI, per Gurman, “is built heavily around photo slideshows and clock displays, similar to the new StandBy Mode on the upcoming iPhone Duo” and users can “swipe up from the clock screen or photos to open the app launcher.”

We’ve seen multiple leaks this past week around this Photo Face in homeOS, as seen below.

Siri AI is the central input method, but Apple apps and a Home Screen will also be available via touch

Siri AI will be central to homeOS interactions. Per Gurman on his new podcast:

The new operating system is basically, what would an OS look like if Siri AI had an OS? If Siri AI was not just an app on the phone, if it wasn’t just an interface on the phone. What if it was an operating system?…It’s all about this concept of personal search and personal context, being able to ask for songs, podcasts, notes, calendar items, photos that are bespoke to you.

Voice won’t be the only interaction method though. Apple apps and a Home Screen will be part of homeOS too. Siri AI can be used to control these apps, but touch input will be supported too.

Built-in homeOS apps will include Music, Podcasts, Photos, Weather, FaceTime, Notes, Calendar, Messages, Reminders, and more. No App Store is expected to be available, but third-party widgets can be brought over from your iPhone.

Like on the current HomePod though, the idea is that most of the time, your interactions with homeOS happen via Siri.

title: iPadOS 27.2: Two new features coming soon to your iPad
snippet: iPadOS 27.2 is coming later this month as a new iPad software update, here are two new features it will bring. more…
fullText:
iPadOS 27.2 is coming later this month as a new iPad software update, here are two new features it will bring.

Siri AI is a major improvement over the old Siri, and I’m using it all the time on my iPad—often with a CMD + Space keyboard shortcut since Siri and Spotlight are now integrated.

In iPadOS 27.2, Apple is introducing another convenient way to interact with Siri that first debuted on the Mac in macOS Golden Gate.

When you select text in iPadOS 27.2 via a trackpad or mouse, there’s a new Siri contextual popup that appears to the left of your selection. If you hover over the Siri icon with your cursor, it instantly expands to offer an ‘Ask Siri’ text field.

This makes it quick and easy to ask Siri about whatever you’ve highlighted. And if you’re in the writing process, the Siri popup even has suggestions like ‘Proofread,’ ‘Rewrite,’ and ‘How does this sound?’ so you can get help with just a click.

#2: Profiles in Apple TV app

iPads make great video devices whether you’re an adult or a kid. And if you share an iPad with a partner or child, the Apple TV app has a welcome addition coming soon: user profiles.

iPadOS 27.2 brings over the same profiles feature that tvOS already offers on Apple TV 4K.

When you open the Apple TV app on iPad, you’ll see a new profile selection screen at startup. From here, you can choose who’s watching and the TV app will automatically update its queue, playback history, and content recommendations based on your selection.

If you’re a parent, profiles will take content restrictions into account. So when your child’s profile is active, they’ll only see films and TV shows that match the age settings you’ve previously set.

title: Googlebooks can’t install the Slack web app on day one
snippet: Googlebook is now on sale and shipping to customers and, on day one at least, they can’t install the Slack web app. more…
fullText:
Googlebook is now on sale and shipping to customers and, on day one at least, they can’t install the Slack web app. 

Googlebook as a platform relies on two main forms of apps. The first is native Android apps, as Googlebook OS is, at its core, Android. That’s what you’ll use for many experiences including Gemini, Google Photos, music apps, and more. Others, like Gmail and YouTube, instead rely on progressive web apps. That term might sound familiar if you’re a long-time Chromebook user, as Chromebooks bet pretty heavily on progressive web apps (PWAs).

That history aside, Googlebooks directly tell their users to use Slack through the web app. The Play Store puts up a banner saying that Slack is “better on the website” when you try to download the Android app. 

That’s correct, frankly, as Slack’s Android app has terrible support for anything besides a standard smartphone. 

	

But the Slack web app cannot be installed on a Googlebook at this time.

	

Trying to install the Slack web app as a PWA on Googlebook results in an error message saying that “this app cannot be installed.” You can still create a shortcut that opens as a Chrome tab, but it won’t open in a window. 

Other PWAs we’ve tested including Photopea, Squoosh, SnapDrop, and others seem to be working fine. It’s unclear why Slack in particular is broken, but it’s hard to imagine it’s the only PWA not working on Googlebook on day one. More importantly, Slack is a mainstay in the modern workspace, so lacking any form of desktop-level Slack support on day one is sure to leave a poor impression on early Googlebook adopters.

Update: Google, in a statement, says that Slack is not a “compliant” PWA but that Googlebook will add support for manual installation soon.

Installing PWAs is fully supported on Googlebooks. But, the Slack web app isn’t a compliant PWA. Chrome on ChromeOS allows manual installation even though it’s not a PWA. This capability will also be coming to Chrome on Googlebooks soon.

That term might sound familiar if you’re a long-time Chromebook user, as Chromebooks bet pretty heavily on progressive web apps (PWAs).

title: macOS 27.2 reveals new clues about Apple’s touchscreen MacBook Pro
snippet: Apple is widely expected to release a new touchscreen MacBook Pro as soon as this month. This will mark the first-ever touchscreen Mac, and Apple is laying the groundwork in macOS 27.2 to accommodate touch gestures. more…
fullText:
Apple is widely expected to release a new touchscreen MacBook Pro as soon as this month. This will mark the first-ever touchscreen Mac, and Apple is laying the groundwork in macOS 27.2 to accommodate touch gestures.

Apple released macOS 27.2 beta 3 to developers today, and it includes new references to upcoming support for touchscreen interactivity. As discovered by Aaron Perris for MacRumors, there are “gesture recognition tools” for several stock Apple apps:

Photos adds “PXGTouchDwellGestureRecognizer”

Notes adds “ICTouchPressGestureRecognizer”

Safari adds “a touch sentinel recognizer”

Quick Look adds a “dragTouch feature”

macOS 27.2 beta 3 also adds a new long-press animation for the Dock, which could also be a hint at the forthcoming touchscreen MacBook Pro:

Apple has gradually made a number of changes to macOS 27 in preparation for touchscreen support, including pull-to-refresh support for the first time. macOS 27 also added touch input to Sidecar, a feature that lets you use your iPad as a secondary display for your Mac.

Bloomberg has also reported on Apple’s work to optimize macOS for the impending touchscreen MacBook Pro. For instance, tapping a button or control will prompt macOS to dynamically display relevant touch options. Similarly, tapping the menu bar will automatically enlarge controls for easier touch navigation.

In addition to a touchscreen, the new MacBook Pro will reportedly have an OLED display and be “significantly lighter” than the current models.

Apple is expected to introduce the new MacBook Pro (or MacBook Ultra?) as soon as this month, though Bloomberg has cautioned it could slip to November.

title: Googlebooks with Intel chipsets might have trouble with ‘complex’ Android apps
snippet: According to a statement from Google, Intel-based Googlebooks will apparently still struggle with some Android apps. more…
fullText:
According to a statement from Google, Intel-based Googlebooks will apparently still struggle with some Android apps.

When Android apps made their debut on ChromeOS, one of the big downsides was that ARM-based machines ran those apps better than those using Intel chips. It was never a surprise given that Android apps are generally designed for devices running on an ARM architecture vs the x86 used on Intel chips.

Yet, the problem remains on Googlebook.

Despite the whole platform being Android-based this time around, Google confirmed in a statement to Android Authority that Intel-based Googlebook machines will still run into the occasional hiccup with “complex” Android apps and games, though the company emphasizes that “the vast majority” will work just fine.

	

The vast majority of Android apps run smoothly across both Intel and Qualcomm Googlebooks right out of the box.

Because many Android apps were originally designed for Arm chips, a small handful of complex apps or games need some developer tuning to run their best on Intel-based platforms. We’re working hand-in-hand with app developers, Intel, and Qualcomm to continuously optimize performance and expand compatibility across the entire portfolio.

	

Still, this is noteworthy as the first wave of Googlebook hardware includes mostly Intel-based machines. Laptops from Lenovo, Asus, and Acer all run on Panther Lake-generation Intel chips, while Dell and HP machines both use the Snapdragon X Elite (the 2024 chip, not the newer version).

Another chip used for Googlebook from MediaTek is also in the works, though no machines are using it just yet.

The first batch of Googlebook laptops are all available as of today.

title: Galaxy S27 series pricing may not only increase, but cost more to upgrade storage
snippet: Samsung’s new Galaxy S27 series is rumored to come at a higher price than previous versions, but that’s no surprise. What’s a little harder to swallow is the larger rumored gap between storage variants, according to one leaker. more…
fullText:
Samsung’s new Galaxy S27 series is rumored to come at a higher price than previous versions, but that’s no surprise. What’s a little harder to swallow is the larger rumored gap between storage variants, according to one leaker.

In succession to the Galaxy S26 lineup, the Galaxy S27 series is expected to take on plenty of physical changes. Namely, in design. Previous leaks have provided CAD renders of the new camera island and overall look, but those have also been caveated with a promised price increase.

Following rumors that the Galaxy S27 Ultra could start at $1,400, a new bit of information has surfaced from a leaker on Naver. According to Lanzuk, the Galaxy S27 series, as a whole, is expected to come at a higher price. The estimated jump is reportedly in the “high 130,000 won range” (~$100). But the post also suggests Samsung is setting a “steeper rate of increase” to the prices of each capacity, likely referring to storage variants.

That could suggest that, instead of a $200 gap between some storage variants, the disparity could expand. Then again, the post isn’t clear on whether this is a linear price increase or one that also increases upgrade costs over previous generations.

	

The posted leak is courtesy of domestic Korean sources, indicating this price increase is specific to Samsung’s home soil. That doesn’t mean it won’t translate to other regions, like the US or Europe.

We’re a bit wary of a report like this. Not because a price increase is unlikely for the Galaxy S27 series – statistically, it very much is – but because of clashing numbers. The previously noted leak also suggested the Galaxy S27 series would remain unchanged as a whole, apart from the most premium flagship model. This leak contradicts that, noting every device will see a jump.

It’s very possible that Samsung is flipping between the two until it ultimately decides on exactly how much it needs to increase the cost of each device and variant to make a profit off of devices stuffed with NAND and LPDDR6 RAM, which the post also notes will be included on “some models.”

Until the Galaxy S27 series launches early next year, there will likely be little confirmation on Samsung’s finalized price increases.

title: I can’t use Apple’s new Screen Time on my daughter’s iPhone because my son won’t update his MacBook
snippet: To update to the revamped Screen Time parental controls, every device in my family group must be on the relevant version 27. And that was just the start of my struggles. | Screenshot by Jennifer Pattison Tuohy / The Verge After suffering years of frustration with Apple's parental control features, I've been eagerly anticipating the revamped Screen Time that launched last month with iOS 27. Unfortunately, I can't use it. Technically, this is because my 18-year-old son hasn't got round to updating his MacBook. But mostly, it's because Apple's rollout of the new feature has been confusing and frustrating, with fiddly requirements that might have you digging through drawers for your old devices. "We're working to resolve delays some families are seeing." Katie Lowry, Apple spokesperson I'm not even trying to use Screen Time on my son's devices. He's 18, away … Read the full story at The Verge.
fullText:
After suffering years of frustration with Apple’s parental control features, I’ve been eagerly anticipating the revamped Screen Time that launched last month with iOS 27. Unfortunately, I can’t use it.

Technically, this is because my 18-year-old son hasn’t got round to updating his MacBook. But mostly, it’s because Apple’s rollout of the new feature has been confusing and frustrating, with fiddly requirements that might have you digging through drawers for your old devices.

“We’re working to resolve delays some families are seeing.”

— Katie Lowry, Apple spokesperson

I’m not even trying to use Screen Time on my son’s devices. He’s 18, away at college, and well beyond my parental controls. The problem is I apparently need him to update his MacBook Neo before I can use Apple’s new Screen Time features on my 15-year-old daughter’s iPhone. His college is four hours away, and like many college kids, he’s an expert at ignoring text messages from his mom asking him to do a boring chore.

My problem stems from Apple’s requirement that, to use the new Screen Time on any device in your connected household, every iPhone, iPad, Apple Watch, Mac, and even Vision Pro in your Apple Family Sharing group has to be updated to the relevant OS 27.

On top of that, if you have older devices that aren’t compatible with the latest OS, you can’t use the new Screen Time on them at all. While Apple says these “legacy devices” won’t prevent you from using the new Screen Time on newer devices, some users are finding they can only turn on the new Screen Time features after deleting the old gadgets from their accounts.

All of this is creating a lot of frustration for parents like me, who just want a reliable, easy way to manage their child’s screen time. I reached out to Apple about the problems I’ve been having, and the company acknowledged the issues, saying it is making changes to “resolve” them.

”This is our biggest child safety update yet, designed to give families even more tools to help keep children safe,” Apple spokesperson Katie Lowry told me. “We’re continuing to improve the rollout of the new parental controls so parents can get set up quickly and easily, and we’re working to resolve delays some families are seeing.”

Apple’s Screen Time is the company’s version of parental controls, and it’s been beset by issues since its introduction in 2018. In the years I’ve been using it, I’ve faced ongoing problems, from settings not syncing reliably across devices to trouble managing contacts and time limits remotely. And of course, my children finding ways to override my settings, thanks to Reddit threads, YouTube videos, and annoyingly good guesses.

When Apple dedicated a big slice of its 2026 WWDC keynote to Screen Time, I was hopeful it meant the company had taken parent feedback seriously and was building a more robust and easier-to-use experience. The updates and new features look promising, but I haven’t been able to try them because of the ongoing setup issues. And I’m not alone.

To use the new Screen Time on any device in your Family Sharing group every device has to be updated to OS 27

Alongside the roadblock with my son’s MacBook Neo (which, admittedly, is on us), I’ve run into several other hurdles while trying to access the new Screen Time.

There’s the problem that Apple thinks my Mac Mini, which I updated to macOS 27 over a week ago, is still on macOS 26. There’s the problem of my sixth-gen iPad Mini that I handed down to my son, but which Apple still lists under my name and as running iPadOS 18. Then there’s the problem that my daughter’s iPad Pro is too old to update to the latest software.

To reiterate, to use the new Screen Time on any device, every eligible device has to be updated to OS 27, because the new Screen Time uses a completely redesigned iCloud architecture.

My son’s iPad Mini is compatible, and I updated it when he was last home (without his MacBook). But when I went to enable the new Screen Time controls again, Apple showed that same iPad Mini under my account as needing to be updated. That iPad obviously doesn’t exist: a ghost iPad, you might say. Eventually, removing it from my account fixed the problem (Settings > Apple Account > Devices > Remove Device), but it took several attempts digging through menus, plus waiting a full weekend for it to clear.

In fact, all my attempts to conform to Apple’s requirements for the new Screen Time have taken a while to kick in. It seems there’s a delay between updating a device and the service becoming available. My editor updated all his devices but still didn’t have access. It was only after waiting and removing all his legacy devices — those that can’t be updated to 27 — from his account that the option appeared.

It’s unclear whether it was time or his actions that led to his eventual success. Apple’s documentation says legacy devices shouldn’t stop you from using the new Screen Time on compatible devices, but some Reddit users also found that removing them unlocked access. Either way, Apple needs to make this whole process clearer so families don’t give up on trying to access what I hope are valuable features.

The fact that these legacy devices can’t use the new Screen Time features raises a bigger issue. Passing older devices down to children is common in families, and the requirement to be on version 27 will mean many kids’ devices won’t get access to the improved parental controls.

For example, my daughter’s third-gen iPad Pro (a hand-me-down from my husband) taps out at iPadOS 26, meaning it can’t ever run the new Screen Time. So, she will have one device (her iPhone 15) that can use the new Screen Time and one device (her iPad) that can’t. I won’t know how this will work until I have access, but my guess is it won’t be fun.

My guess is that I’ll have to use the old Screen Time directly on the iPad, rather than managing it from my phone as I do now. This is because it won’t be compatible with the upgraded iCloud architecture that syncs settings between devices in your family group. If you have multiple older devices, you may want to just stick with the old Screen Time controls for now.

My son might be suspicious of my request to update his device so I can use Screen Time on his sister’s iPhone.

In the meantime, I’m still trying to figure out what bug is causing my Mac Mini to block the update, while continuing to nag my son to update his MacBook Neo. College is a fun, busy time, and “update software on my computer” is low on his to-do list. But his reticence just might stem from being slightly suspicious of my request to update his device so I can use Screen Time on his sister’s iPhone.

Technology certainly has added another tricky layer to the parent-child relationship. After a decade of attempting to balance giving my kids access to the benefits of technology with keeping them safe and teaching them healthy habits, I’m frankly exhausted. I have a couple of years left in my struggle, but the irony of this situation isn’t lost on me; that the system meant to protect one child now depends on the goodwill of the other, who is totally over it.

title: What has been the best Google Pixel to date? [Poll]
snippet: On 4 October 2016, Google introduced the original Pixel and Pixel XL, marking a major pivot away from the developer-focused Nexus line and ushering in what is now a decade of “Made by Google” hardware – but which is best and why? more…
fullText:
On 4 October 2016, Google introduced the original Pixel and Pixel XL, marking a major pivot away from the developer-focused Nexus line and ushering in what is now a decade of “Made by Google” hardware – but which is best and why?

Over the past 10 years, the lineup has expanded from a pair of traditional slab smartphones to a product portfolio that includes foldable devices, watches, earbuds, a single tablet, and budget-focused A-series models, culminating in the Pixel 11 series.

I’m biased, I think that the 4a is the best of the bunch, but determining which device holds the title of the best Pixel to date is going to be a fun, healthy debate for those of us who have used more than a few of the lineup over the years, especially as not all have been covered in glory.

The initial breakthrough

The original Pixel and Pixel XL established Google’s focus on camera processing and clean software integration. While the launch models lacked water resistance and stereophonic audio, their computational photography capabilities set a new baseline for mobile imaging.

	

A year later, the Pixel 2 and Pixel 2 XL introduced the iconic “Panda” design and front-facing stereo speakers. Although the LG-manufactured Pixel 2 XL faced criticism regarding display viewing angles, the series remains highly regarded for solidifying Google’s image processing dominance.

The Pixel 3 and 3 XL introduced Night Sight and a dedicated Pixel Visual Core chip, alongside dual front-facing cameras with an ultra-wide sensor. Despite memory management limits tied to its 4GB of RAM and the prominent display notch on the XL model, the third-generation devices brought significant refinements to software performance. Shortly after, the Pixel 3a series created the mid-range budget category for Google, pairing flagship camera capabilities with lower price points.

Pivots, Experiments, and Design Changes

Google shifted its approach with the Pixel 4 and 4 XL, introducing Soli radar gesture controls, 90Hz Motion Sense displays, and the only instance of 3D Face Unlock. The removal of the rear fingerprint scanner and poor battery life on the smaller model limited its appeal, though the 4 XL maintains a loyal following for its build, slim profile, and biometric features.

The 4a and 4a 5G focused back on value during a period of transition. That path culminated in the Pixel 5, which abandoned high-end flagship processors in favor of a mid-range Qualcomm Snapdragon 765G chipset, a uniform-bezel design, a rear fingerprint sensor, and a high-density battery. The Pixel 5a with 5G followed a similar template with a larger form factor and water resistance.

The Pixel 6 and 6 Pro marked the biggest moment in the lineup since its inception. Introducing custom Google Tensor silicon, a horizontal camera bar design, the series briefly pushed Google back into true flagship territory. The subsequent Pixel 6a brought this design language and processor to the A-series lineup, but had the killer addition of the best Tensor chip at a time when most mid-rangers were still forgoing high-end SoCs in favor of middling performance.

Refinement continued with the Pixel 7 and 7 Pro, which upgraded to the Tensor G2, addressed thermal efficiency, and refreshed the camera bar with an aluminum finish. The 7a brought high-refresh-rate screens and wireless charging to the lower price bracket for the first time.

Expanding Form Factors and Beyond

Google’s smartphone ecosystem expanded significantly with the introduction of the Pixel Fold and the Pixel Tablet. The Fold represented Google’s entry into flexible displays with a wider outer screen, while the Pixel Tablet offered a dual-purpose home display experience via its charging speaker dock.

The Pixel 8 and 8 Pro introduced seven years of OS updates, Tensor G3 silicon, brighter Actua displays, and a flat screen design for the Pro model. The 8a brought those long-term software commitments to a lower price point and arguably blurred the lines between the A-series and the base model for the first time.

	

The Pixel 9 series expanded the lineup further, introducing a third flagship size with the Pixel 9, Pixel 9 Pro, and Pixel 9 Pro XL, alongside the refined Pixel 9 Pro Fold. The series introduced updated industrial design with flattened sides, updated Tensor G4 chips, and satellite connectivity.

Since the 9 was launched, we’ve had a couple of years of effectively the same device with minor iterations. Most of the changes have been focused solely on hardware efficiency and processing performance.

Reaching the 10-year mark, the Pixel 11 series builds upon that decade of iterations. From off-the-shelf components to custom chips that may not have quite hit the heights many have wanted, there’s never a dull moment with a Google phone, for better or worse.

Which device stands out as the best release over the last 10 years? We’ve omitted wearables in a bid to streamline the entire poll, but be sure to cast your vote in the poll below and let us know the reasons behind your choice in the comments.

title: Ready for Driverless Trucks? I Took a Ride in Kodiak’s Autonomous Semi
snippet: Kodiak is planning to bring its fully self-driving trucks to highways later this year. I took a test ride to see the technology in action.
fullText:
Despite the growing number of players in the space, self-driving vehicles remain far from ubiquitous. In places like the San Francisco Bay Area, hailing a robotaxi is now nearly as easy as requesting an Uber. But in most cities, driverless cars have yet to surface at all.

Still, autonomous vehicles of all sizes and purposes continue to crop up in various regions. Kodiak AI is one company looking to shake up transportation and shipping in the near future. Founded in 2018, it set out to deploy semi trucks on highways without a human behind the wheel, and it’s getting close to realizing that vision.

The company’s autonomous driving system, called the Kodiak Driver, launched in December 2024, and has so far been deployed in 35 fully driverless trucks, which are owned and operated by Atlas Energy Solutions in the Permian Basin in New Mexico and Texas. The trucks haul frac sand, typically used during hydraulic fracking to help keep fractures in rock formations open, from depots to well sites.

Kodiak plans to deploy its self-driving trucks on highways in Texas by the end of the year.Celso Bulgatti/CNET

Now, Kodiak wants to bring its fully driverless operations to the highway, starting in Texas with services for furniture giant Ikea later this year. That route will operate between Houston and Dallas, spanning 219 miles primarily along Interstate 45.

Massive trucks barreling down highways without a driver may be a daunting vision, but Michael Wiesinger, Kodiak’s chief operating officer, says they’ll make transportation more reliable and efficient.

“Lots of people, unfortunately, are getting killed in traffic, and many of those are related to truck accidents,” he said. “An autonomous truck [has a] 360-degree view of the world, [and] will actually never get drowsy, never get tired, never get distracted. They will make transportation safer.”

This is the sensor pod that houses the cameras, lidar and radar.Abrar Al-Heeti/CNET

In California, Kodiak’s driverless tech is already being used to ship produce from Fresno to Los Angeles, though a safety driver remains behind the wheel, ready to take over as needed.

I visited Kodiak’s headquarters in Mountain View, California, to ride in one of the company’s trucks and see its autonomous tech in action. As per current state regulations, there was still a safety operator onboard, ready to take control of the wheel if necessary. I wasn’t exactly nervous, but his presence nevertheless helped to assuage any trepidation, given how much bigger a semi truck is than a robotaxi from Waymo or Zoox.

During the demonstration, the Kodiak truck easily navigated surface streets, including making tight turns and dodging rows of parallel-parked cars and trailers. We made our way to the highway on-ramp rather slowly and carefully, picking up speed to 55 mph once we hit the roadway. When we really got going, it all felt remarkably ordinary, with the truck weaving through lanes and dodging construction cones without any trouble. After about 20 minutes, the truck navigated to an exit and we made our way back to Kodiak’s HQ. 

Kodiak’s trucks run on diesel — the standard for heavy-duty commercial trucking — which allows them to travel over longer distances than if they were electric, the company notes.

The inside of the Kodiak semi feels standard — apart from the screen showing what the vehicle sees as it navigates autonomously.Celso Bulgatti/CNET

The growth of driverless operations brings with it mounting concern about lost jobs. Kodiak says deploying autonomous vehicles doesn’t mean humans won’t be involved at all.

“Before launching an autonomous truck, it gets inspected, it gets fueled, it gets prepared for the run,” Wiesinger said. “Those preparations are done by humans on the ground.”

He added that Kodiak is collaborating with truck-stop providers to help with refueling as it plans to eventually expand its driverless range across thousands of miles.

Kodiak isn’t the only company working on autonomous trucking. Other players include Aurora, Waabi and Gatik, while Tesla is making a push into this space as well with its all-electric Tesla Semi, which could one day adopt driverless capabilities, too.

Before climbing aboard Kodiak’s semi, it was hard to fathom how a Class 8 heavy-duty truck could navigate the complexities of residential streets and highways. As we passed other cars, I found myself wondering whether those drivers and passengers realized they were sharing the road with what could be the future of long-haul trucking. Then again, some of those folks were cruising in a Waymo robotaxi, so perhaps the existence of autonomous trucks won’t be such a tough pill to swallow for everyone.

Check out the video above for my ride-along in Kodiak’s self-driving truck.

				

					

						

													

					

					

						

Abrar Al-Heeti
						

						

							Senior Technology Reporter						
					

											

								

											Abrar's interests include phones, streaming, autonomous vehicles, internet trends, entertainment, pop culture and digital accessibility. In addition to her current role, she's worked for CNET's video, culture and news teams. She graduated with bachelor's and master's degrees in journalism from the University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign. Though Illinois is home, she now loves San Francisco -- steep inclines and all.

title: I’ve Been Testing Kitchen Gear for Years. Here Are 4 Prime Day Deals I’m Texting to Friends
snippet: Some of of the best kitchen gear we’ve tested from Vitamix, Moccamaster and Ninja are at all-time low prices.
fullText:
Amazon’s October Prime sales are a chance to outfit your kitchen with sought-after items without paying full price. With everything more expensive, you’d be wise to take advantage of discounts if you’re hoping to upgrade your coffee maker, air fryer, blender and other helpful cooking equipment.

There’s a lot to parse, with thousands of deals on Amazon and plenty of knock-offs that look tempting but may not be worth it even at a discount. I’ve been testing kitchen gear for years and know how to spot a great kitchen deal through the smoke and mirrors. Of the hundreds I sifted through, these are the four I’d recommend to friends, family or anyone gift shopping for a home cook — established or aspiring.

	

		

	

									

									

						

	

				

			Vitamix		

	

		

							

											

							$295 (save $205)						

											

							Vitamix Propel Series 510 blender						

									

			

	

			

			

				Get it now			

		

					
			

				

All Vitamix blenders pack big power, but the Propel Series has a little extra — at least compared to the VX series (formerly called the Explorian). It has 2.2 peak horsepower, so it can handle just about anything you drop inside. Unlike the manual-only VX, the Propel has three built-in automatic programs for smoothies, frozen desserts and hot soups for hands-off blending. It’s also one of the quietest and lightest Vitamix blenders, which makes it feel user-friendly. These blenders aren’t cheap, but as CNET’s Anna Gragert, who uses a 19-year-old Vitamix without issue, can attest, they really last. 

			

		
					
			

					This is the cheapest we've ever seen the Vitamix Propel 510 drop on Amazon. The powerful blender retails for $500 with an average tag of $433 on Amazon. It's only been down to $300 twice before during flash sales. It comes with a five-year warranty. 				

		

	

		

	

									

									

						

	

				

			Pamela Vachon/CNET		

	

		

							

											

							$153 (save $27)						

											

							Ninja Crispi glass-bowl air fryer						

									

			

	

			

			

				Get it now			

		

					
			

					

Simply put, this is the best air fryer we’ve tested, and it’s currently at its lowest price ever on Amazon. The Crispi broke the air fryer mold when it launched, with a modular build that’s easier to store and a glass bowl cooking chamber that’s easy to clean and PFAS-free. If you’ve used a nonstick air fryer basket, you know how quickly it accumulates a layer of gunk that’s hard to remove. Not so with the Crispi. As a bonus, the cooking chamber comes with a tight-fitting lid that makes storing leftover food simple and intuitive. 

The Crispi has as much power as you’ll ever need from an air fryer and features uncomplicated cooking controls. If there is one ding on this model, it’s that the cooking chamber is lower than some we’ve tested, meaning you might struggle to fit a whole chicken or large cut of meat without breaking it down first. For more cooking capacity, try the Ninja Crispi Pro — also on sale for Prime Day.
