			Technivorm		

	

		

							

											

							$270 (save $100)						

											

							Technivorm Moccamaster KBGV coffee maker						

									

			

	

			

			

				Get it now			

		

					
			

					

The Dutch coffee maker company Technivorm has sold exceptional brewers for decades, earning it cult status among coffee snobs. The KBGV drip coffee machine has clean lines and sharp angles that give off both a vintage and laboratory feel. Retro design aside, in our testing, this brewer consistently delivers perfectly balanced coffee, heating water up to a precise temperature as it hits the grounds. 

				

		
					
			

					Technivorm's brewers often sell for $400, so snatching up one of its most popular models for $270 is a no-brainer if you were already planning to upgrade your home setup. The KBGV is currently listed for $366 on Amazon and seldom drops below $300.				

		

	

		

	

									

									

						

	

				

			Ninja/CNET		

	

		

							

											

							$88 (save $42)						

											

							Ninja Blendboss personal blender						

									

			

	

			

			

				Get it now			

		

					
			

				

The BlendBoss is the latest addition to Ninja’s blender lineup, and it quickly became our top pick. When we tested it against several others, we found it pulverized ice into snow in 15 seconds — as fast as any — and made quick work of turning dense frozen fruit into healthy smoothies. The blender comes in a range of colors — great for gifting — and has a quirky design unlike any other personal blender I’ve seen. 

			

		
					
			

					This is one of few times the BlendBoss has been discounted since it launched earlier this year. The small and powerful blender typically sells for $130 but it's down to $88 for Prime Day. 				

		

What’s the single best kitchen deal?

That largely depends on your kitchen needs. For me, the powerful Vitamix Propel 510 for $295 is simply one of the best prices we’ve seen on any of the brand’s iconic blenders in some time. I fully expect that deal to expire or sell out long before Prime Day ends. 

			

More from CNET

Is Prime Day a good time to buy kitchen gadgets?

Absolutely. The kitchen category really pops off during Prime Day sales, and we’re seeing discounts of 40% to 60% on some of our favorite gear, making them easy to recommend right now.  The next opportunity to save big will be Black Friday, but price hikes can happen at any time, so there’s no guarantee we’ll see deals as good as today’s again.

title: iPhone 18 Pro Max Can’t Make a Call on AT&T? Apple Says It Will Replace It for Free
snippet: A software and carrier settings update should prevent future problems, but people who have been affected will need a replacement phone.
fullText:
Some owners of Apple’s new iPhone 18 Pro Max may be enjoying the new camera system and improved battery life. But if they’re AT&T customers, they could find the phone unable to perform its most essential task: making calls. That also includes being able to dial 911 in emergencies. The fix appears to be a pair of Apple updates rolling out on Friday – but anyone who has already been affected by the problem will need a replacement phone, according to Apple. An Apple representative says the company will replace those phones for free.

Last week, some iPhone 18 Pro Max owners on AT&T’s network reported no cellular access. MacRumors reported that AT&T sent a text message this week to iPhone 18 Pro Max owners, encouraging them to update to iOS 27.0.1 immediately. MacRumors estimates that thousands of customers have been affected.

On Friday, Apple said it’s issuing a separate carrier-settings patch to pair with the iOS 27.0.1 update. But the patch comes too late for certain owners of the new phone.

			

More from CNET

An Apple representative told CNET that the updates are intended to guard against this problem in the future and won’t fix the situation for iPhone 18 Pro Max owners who are already experiencing it. Apple will provide a new phone free of charge to those owners. Affected customers should contact Apple Support or AT&T.

In Reddit threads about the issue, some owners report that the 27.0.1 update by itself did not fix the problem, nor did upgrading to the public beta of iOS 27.2.

Only the iPhone 18 Pro Max is affected

So far, the issue seems limited to iPhone 18 Pro Max models on AT&T’s network. I reached out to contacts at T-Mobile and Verizon, and both report they’re not seeing similar reports on their networks. I haven’t experienced the issue on an iPhone 18 Pro that runs on AT&T’s network, which isn’t surprising given that this particular problem affects iPhone 18 Pro Max units, not iPhone 18 Pro phones. A CNET colleague’s iPhone 18 Pro Max on Google Fi (which uses T-Mobile’s network) is not experiencing the issue.

It’s unclear whether the lack of connectivity is related to the phone’s hardware. While the standard iPhone 18 Pro is equipped with Apple’s C2 modem, the iPhone 18 Pro Max in the US is the only model with Qualcomm’s Snapdragon X80 modem, as shown in this teardown of the phone by iFixIt. Qualcomm has been Apple’s modem provider for years, but Apple has worked to move away from relying on the third party for the essential phone component. That relationship is due to expire this year.

According to a TechInsights iPhone 18 Pro Max teardown, the X80 modem is also used in the iPhone 17 Pro and iPhone 17 Pro Max, but a new millimeter-wave antenna has been added to the 18 Pro Max. Millimeter-wave offers much faster data speeds in areas where the technology is installed, but it can have a shorter range and be reduced by obstacles. Apple’s C2 modem also includes a millimeter-wave antenna.

A representative from Qualcomm didn’t immediately respond to a request for comment.

fullText:
A new market intelligence report says that the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max are selling well in China, making Apple the best-selling brand in the country during the launch week.

title: Pixel Recorder makes it easier to access audio files
snippet: Pixel Recorder is getting a small quality-of-life update that surfaces your audio files to other apps on your device. more…
fullText:
Pixel Recorder is getting a small quality-of-life update that surfaces your audio files to other apps on your device.

Previously, accessing the actual audio file involved opening a recording and then the share menu for the “Audio or transcript file” option. This took you to the system share sheet for a manual save. 

Pixel Recorder now has an “Access recordings in other apps” setting that lets you “View your recordings in the Files app or other apps for easier access.” 

This is enabled by default, with a prompt on the homepage announcing the new feature: “Access recordings in other apps. Manage this in Settings anytime.”

	

The new “Recordings” folder on your device shows all audio that you’ve recorded or downloaded from the cloud.

Version 4.2.20260823.x of Pixel Recorder widely rolls out this capability.

It follows the last update in August that introduced the new app icon, which is not yet live (along with Weather) on the Pixel Watch. Recorder will also be available on Googlebooks going forward.

title: iOS 27 upgrades Messages app with key new features for RCS
snippet: iOS 27 includes several welcome additions to the Messages app, including two key upgrades for RCS conversations. Here’s what’s new. more…
fullText:
iOS 27 includes several welcome additions to the Messages app, including two key upgrades for RCS conversations. Here’s what’s new.

iOS 27 makes RCS better in Messages with inline replies and improved Tapback reactions

Apple’s Messages app benefits from a variety of new features in iOS 27, like more personalized Smart Replies, a Drawing app perfect for iPhone Duo, and more.

But some of the best upgrades might be related to RCS.

iOS 27 offers improved RCS support thanks to two new features:

Inline replies

Full Tapback support

These changes are part of the RCS 2.7 standard, but Apple hadn’t implemented them until now.

Inline replies work just like in iMessage, letting you reply to a specific message and have it appear inline for all iPhone and Android users in the conversation.

Thanks to proper Tapback support, Android users will no longer have to see annoying messages like “Ryan loved an image” when an iPhone user adds a reaction to media.

Per Apple’s iOS 27 user guide, Messages now supports the following RCS features: “read receipts, typing indicators, Tapbacks, inline replies, and high-resolution photos and videos.”

With these latest RCS upgrades, alongside end-to-end encryption support that launched earlier in the year, RCS is a lot closer to replicating the iMessage experience.

title: Google Wallet for Android adds 12th digital state ID
snippet: Following the last launch at the end of August, Google Wallet is rolling out support for Oklahoma state IDs on Android. more…
fullText:
Following the last launch at the end of August, Google Wallet is rolling out support for Oklahoma state IDs on Android.

Open Google Wallet on your phone and tap the ‘plus’ button next to “View more” at the bottom > IDs & personal info > Driver’s license or state ID. This reveals Oklahoma as the 13th Google Wallet option. It joins Arizona, Arkansas, California, Colorado, Georgia, Iowa, Maryland, Montana, New Mexico, North Dakota, Ohio, and Puerto Rico.

The card design shows the American Bison (state animal) and the scissor-tailed flycatcher (state bird).

The set-up process requires taking photos of the front and back of your physical card, as well as a short video of your face for verification that gets sent to the SOK. This review can take a few minutes with a notification confirming once it’s available. You’ll also get an email confirmation from the state agency.

	

First, tap on the reader or scan your QR code: Your personal info won’t be shared yet. On your phone, review what info you want to share.

Next, review what info will be shared: Make sure you’re comfortable sharing the info they request

You don’t need to hand your phone to anyone: Your ID will be securely shared using Bluetooth, so make sure it’s on

Lastly, verify it’s you to share your info: For extra security, verify that this ID is yours using your face, fingerprint, password, or PIN

“Details” next to “Show code” lets you enable an “Activity history,” while “Driver’s License information” lists license number, date of expiry, address, and more.

IDs can be read via NFC or by having the QR code scanned. It is accepted at some airports by the TSA. Officially, you still have to carry your ID card as the one on your phone “does not replace the requirement for individuals to carry a physical card.” 

Your device must be running Android 8+ and have a screen lock, with Bluetooth and Nearby devices enabled. A state ID can be deleted from Google Wallet at any time or remotely via myaccount.google.com. As a private pass, it does not get synced to the cloud and is only available on one device.

Tap Personal Info.

Scroll to “Digital ID.”

Tap Manage Digital ID.

Next to the ID or license that you want to remove, tap Delete.

Confirm that you want to delete your ID from your device and Google Account.

snippet: There’s very little left of the Galaxy S27 Ultra left to surface before launch, but new information might change what to expect in Samsung’s device color options. more…
fullText:
There’s very little left of the Galaxy S27 Ultra left to surface before launch, but new information might change what to expect in Samsung’s device color options.

According to a short and straightforward post on Twitter/X by @UniverseIce, the Galaxy S27 Ultra series will come in four base color variants – Black, Blue, Light Pink, and White. That doesn’t include the Samsung online exclusive colorways, which usually add a couple of hues to the lineup.

Previous leaks claimed Samsung would offer the Galaxy S27 Ultra in five colors, all of the above included except Purple. It’s unclear whether a purple version was excluded this time around, or if Samsung plans to sell the version as an online-exclusive. It would be a first in four years if Samsung didn’t release a purple Galaxy S Ultra phone. The Galaxy S23 Ultra in 2023 came in Lavender, and since then, every Galaxy S Ultra phone has been available in some similar shade.

	

It’s worth a quick note that Light Pink comes so very close to Lavender on the color wheel, so do with that information what you will.

In combination with the new camera bar, the Galaxy S27 Ultra will take on an entirely new look. Its design is set rather far from the look of nearly every Galaxy S Ultra phone since 2021, thanks to the camera island spanning the entire rear panel.

Whether you like it or not, the Galaxy S27 Ultra will look like an entirely different phone. And now, it will look different in LavenderLight Pink.

title: Fantastical’s long-awaited Android debut begins today on Googlebook
snippet: Fantastical has long been hailed as one of the greatest calendar apps available today, but if you’re an Android user, there’s a good chance you’ve never used it. Despite a move from Apple exclusivity to cross-platform availability on Windows, Android has long eluded the attention of development team Flexibits. Today, that’s finally changing, as Fantastical is headed to Google’s mobile OS platform — but not precisely in the way you might expect. more…
fullText:
Fantastical has long been hailed as one of the greatest calendar apps available today, but if you’re an Android user, there’s a good chance you’ve never used it. Despite a move from Apple exclusivity to cross-platform availability on Windows, Android has long eluded the attention of development team Flexibits. Today, that’s finally changing, as Fantastical is headed to Google’s mobile OS platform — but not precisely in the way you might expect.

Beginning today, Fantastical is now available for Google’s new laptop initiative, Googlebook. Existing Fantastical users who rely on the app on different platforms (like iOS or Windows) can access Fantastical on Googlebook at no additional charge, while new users coming to Fantastical for the very first time can likewise also use the application on any of their other supported devices.

While the underlying OS on Googlebook is Android, Flexibits’ co-founder and CEO Michael Simmons stressed that the application isn’t quite ready yet to debut on phones, tablets, or foldables. Those versions are on the way — bucking what Simmons himself said back in 2024 when he declared the app would never find its way to the Play Store — but they won’t be ready for launch until sometime in 2027. Likewise, today’s announcement does not include bringing the company’s contact management app, Cardhop, to Android; Simmons tells me they have “no announcement” about that app at this time.

Fantastical began life on Mac back in 2011, offering calendar creation tools via a straightforward ordinary language-based interface that isn’t all too dissimilar to today’s LLMs. Though Flexibits unveiled a Windows variant in late 2024, today’s move marks the first step towards compatibility with Google’s mobile OS, and you can thank Googlebooks for building that bridge. Simmons told me development began after Google showed the Fantastical team a demo of its new laptop platform, and he found himself impressed enough to take a chance on finally expanding the app to Android.

	

While most users will have to wait until next year to get their hands on Fantastical, all you early Googlebook adopters out there have the chance to begin using a brand-new calendar app starting today. Individual pricing starts at $57 per year, with family plans starting at $90 annually. A free, less powerful tier is also available.

title: Apple must pay Masimo an extra $184M for Apple Watch patent infringement
snippet: It’s almost a year since Apple was found to have infringed a Masimo patent for low-power pulse oximeter features used in the Apple Watch. At the time, the company was ordered to pay $634 million in damages, but a federal judge has now ordered it to pay an additional $184 million in interest … more…
fullText:
It’s almost a year since Apple was found to have infringed a Masimo patent for low-power pulse oximeter features used in the Apple Watch.

At the time, the company was ordered to pay $634 million in damages, but a federal judge has now ordered it to pay an additional $184 million in interest …

Apple had been fighting with health tech company Masimo on a couple of fronts. The more serious of them was an International Trade Commission ruling that Apple must remove the blood oxygen feature in two Apple Watch models back in 2023 in order to allow them to be sold in the US. The Cupertino company was forced to redesign the way the feature worked in order to be allowed to bring the devices into the US.

But the company also faced a lawsuit from Masimo, seeking damages for the use of its patented approach to measuring blood oxygen in a power-efficient way. Apple was found to have infringed on this patent and ordered to pay damages amounting to the license fees it should have paid.

Bloomberg Law reports that Apple has now been ordered to pay an additional £184 million in interest on this sum. 

Judge James V. Selna rejected Apple’s argument that awarding interest would constitute a windfall for Masimo, citing US Supreme Court guidance that “interest from the time that the royalty payments would have been received merely serves to make the patent owner whole.”

There was some good news for Apple. Masimo had asked for interest calculated at 7%, but the judge rejected this, saying that the interest rate should instead be equivalent to that paid on Massimo’s own borrowing. However, annual compounding still added a total of $184M to the amount due.

title: Why the Moon Is a Legal Wild West
snippet: Private companies are taking cremated remains and stunt payloads to the moon. Former NASA attorney Steve Mirmina warns that there’s nothing stopping them.
fullText:
For $3,495, you can send your pet’s ashes to the moon. 

Celestis calls itself “the most compelling pet memorial service on or off the planet,” allowing customers to send a “symbolic portion” of their pet’s ashes to live forever on the lunar surface. (Prices are the same for human remains, Celestis says.) It’s part of a growing wave of companies looking to capitalize on the regulatory gray area that the moon inhabits. 

A Japanese beverage company sent up a payload that looked like one of its Pocari Sweat energy drinks in 2014. Artist Jeff Koons sent up 125 mini-sculptures in 2024; each one corresponded to an NFT that collectors could purchase back on Earth. One man has even raised $227,000 to put a giant cross on the moon. All told, humans have left nearly 500,000 pounds of stuff on the moon’s surface to date, most of which consists of government-sent lunar landers, surveyors and other dead spacecraft.

			

More from CNET

This explosion of commercial lunar activity is technically legal, says Steve Mirmina, a professor of space law at Georgetown University and former NASA attorney. 

“I searched and searched the law, and unfortunately, there’s no law against launching race cars,” he said, referring to Elon Musk’s launching of a Tesla Roadster in 2018. “We don’t have a government agency with the legal authority to regulate what happens on the moon.”

Existing US law doesn’t sufficiently regulate what we actually send to the lunar surface, Mirmina argues in Lawful but Awful: U.S. Regulation of Commercial Activities on the Lunar Surface, published Sept. 19 in Air and Space Law. Without a more sustainable legal framework, we risk turning the moon into “Earth’s junk drawer.” 

Who regulates the moon?

To date, 118 countries are parties to the Outer Space Treaty, which was originally enacted in 1967 during the height of the Cold War. It stipulates that space is free for use by all countries, and that they have a duty to avoid harmful contamination in space. 

The 2020 Artemis Accords further enshrined norms of space sustainability into international law. While not legally binding, it constitutes “soft law” norms that shape best practices in space. 

Countries are left to enforce compliance on the private space companies within their borders. In the US, the Federal Aviation Administration governs rocket launches, and NASA’s Commercial Lunar Payload Services program partners with American companies to deliver payloads to the moon. But Congress hasn’t given any one agency the authority to regulate what private companies are actually putting on those payloads. 

“It’s not very useful that they can regulate launch if they can’t regulate what happens after the rocket’s in space,” said Mirmina. “Basically, NASA, the FAA, even the State Department – they’re all kind of pointing at each other, hoping somebody did something. And then nobody had the legal authority to do anything.”

Real-world costs of unchecked commercialization

No one wants to gaze up at the night sky and see an energy drink advertisement. None of this activity has affected our view of the moon so far, and most of it falls into the “annoying” category more than the “truly reprehensible.” But Mirmina worries that there’s no legal safeguard in place to halt some truly awful conduct. 

What’s happening on the moon right now has already stirred outrage from a number of different groups. Navajo Nation President Buu Nygren wrote a letter to NASA in 2023 asking the agency to stop sending human remains to the moon.

“It is crucial to emphasize that the Moon holds a sacred position in many Indigenous cultures, including ours,” Nygren wrote. “The act of depositing human remains and other materials, which could be perceived as discards in any other location, on the moon is tantamount to desecration of this sacred space.”

There’s also the question of how to be good caretakers for future generations. Moon landings produce something called “plume–surface interactions,” in which exhaust from descending spacecraft kicks up rocks and dust at speeds faster than a bullet. When new payloads land with increasing frequency, yesterday’s pet ashes or energy drink advertisements could become tomorrow’s projectiles. Unlike on Earth, the moon has a very thin atmosphere with little erosion, so every item placed on the surface stays “forever,” as Celestis promises customers.

“They become shrapnel for future lunar missions,” Mirmina says. “It’s just a lot easier to prevent it than it’s going to ever be to try to clean it up.”

Stewardship before it’s too late

Everything is hard in space, especially agreeing on the right way to behave in a domain that seems so distant and invulnerable. But it’s also one corner of the government with rare bipartisan approval: Roughly three-quarters of Americans have a favorable opinion of NASA, and seven in 10 say it is essential that the US continue to be a world leader in space, according to the Pew Research Center. Most also support NASA’s goal of sending astronauts back to the moon in 2028.

“Before we’ve really even explored the moon, we’re already tossing up junk to live on there forever,” Mirmina says. “If you care about space or stewardship or the environment, we should preserve it for future explorers and not ruin it before they get there.”

				

					

						

													

					

					

						

Joe Supan
						

						

							Senior Writer						
					

											

								

											Joe Supan is a senior writer for CNET covering home technology, broadband, and moving. Prior to joining CNET, Joe led MyMove's moving coverage and reported on broadband policy, the digital divide, and privacy issues for the broadband marketplace Allconnect. He has been featured as a guest columnist on Broadband Breakfast, and his work has been referenced by the Los Angeles Times, Forbes, National Geographic, Yahoo! Finance and more.

title: Google’s original Pixel Fold was the right idea years ahead of its time
snippet: Google’s original Pixel Fold was inherently flawed but also fundamentally way better than I expected and, thanks to recent arrivals, also way ahead of its time. more…
fullText:
Google’s original Pixel Fold was inherently flawed but also fundamentally way better than I expected and, thanks to recent arrivals, also way ahead of its time.

Foldables were still very much going through growing pains in 2023 when Google stepped up to the plate with its first foldable, the Pixel Fold. At the time, I called it “better than it should be, but far from perfect,” and I stand by that. Even with hindsight of three more Google foldables and the rapid improvements of the rest of the industry, the Pixel Fold managed to do a lot right at the time. It offered sturdy hardware, respectable cameras, and less compromises than most other foldables of the time.

Has it aged well? Not particularly. The glossy finish to the metal frame remains a fingerprint magnet in the worst kind of way, and the sheer heft of this phone is wild. I don’t often take issue with a heavy smartphone, but especially compared to the Galaxy Z Fold 8 I’ve been using the past couple of months, the original Pixel Fold is noticeably heavy in the hand. The crease down the center is huge, and it’s a thick device too. And, three years later, I can only imagine how bad Tensor G2’s heat management issues have become – that was ultimately the deal-breaker for me when I was using the device last. 

Yet, for everything it got wrong, the Pixel Fold got one thing right, the form factor.

	

In the wake of Apple’s debut in the foldable market, brands are quickly pivoting to wider form factors, and they seem to be resonating with customers. The Galaxy Z Fold 8 is a smash hit, and I bet we’ll be seeing a lot more of these wide foldables over the next year. 

But the Pixel Fold did it three years ago, albeit with a lot less flash. 

Google’s foldable looks almost normal compared to a Galaxy Z Fold 8, but the core idea is the same. The wider canvas is designed for better multitasking and tablet apps, something that I pointed out in my original review. Where Samsung’s foldables were really good at using phone apps on a bigger canvas, the Pixel Fold was far more likely to trigger a proper tablet version of an app instead. 

	

Google ultimately threw that away. Why? Android apps simply weren’t ready at the time. While Android apps have always been designed around scaling to form factors, bigger and wider canvases were still in the minority, and most apps didn’t fully support them. As such, the taller and squarish design just made more sense.

Arguably, it still does, but Samsung’s Galaxy Z Fold 8 has shown that it works when you do it “right.” Two months into using it, I’m thrilled with this form factor, and a bit annoyed that Google gave up on it so quickly even though, at the time, it probably made sense. Unfortunately, that’s a bit of a trend in the Pixel’s legacy and Google’s as a whole – Inbox, Stadia, etc. It doesn’t take much to find a Google idea that was left behind too quickly.

It’s anyone’s guess when Google might revisit this design, but I hope it happens.

title: AT&T claims iOS 27.0.1 fixes iPhone 18 Pro Max cellular issues, but users disagree [U]
snippet: Update 1:50 p.m. PT: More details from Apple are available here: Apple confirms iPhone 18 Pro Max AT&T cellular issues, affected devices require hardware replacement Since the iPhone 18 Pro Max launched, some AT&T customers have complained of various connectivity issues. fullText:
Update 1:50 p.m. PT: More details from Apple are available here: 

Apple confirms iPhone 18 Pro Max AT&T cellular issues, affected devices require hardware replacement

Since the iPhone 18 Pro Max launched, some AT&T customers have complained of various connectivity issues.

In a new text message to customers, AT&T says affected users should update their devices to iOS 26.0.1 to fix the issues … but early reports indicate the update doesn’t actually fix the problem.

AT&T tells iPhone 18 Pro Max users to install iOS 27.0.1 

In a thread on Reddit today, an AT&T customer says they received the following automated text message from the carrier:

Hi, it’s AT&T. Action needed: An important Apple software update for your iPhone 18 Pro Max is available. Some phones may be unable to complete calls/text/data, including to 911. Update to iOS 27.0.1 immediately — Settings > General > Software Update. Please contact AT&T or Apple if you have questions.

Apple released iOS 27.0.1 earlier this week. According to the release notes, the update addressed bugs related to Face ID and camera performance for iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max users. The release notes made no mention of any fixes for cellular connectivity problems impacting AT&T customers.

Early reports from AT&T users suggest that iOS 27.0.1 does not fix the connectivity problems affecting iPhone 18 Pro Max. Many affected users say they updated when iOS 27.0.1 was released on Monday and are still facing the same problems.

Affected iPhone 18 Pro Max users can’t connect to AT&T’s network for calls, texts, and data. The users see “SOS” in their iPhone’s status bar. The connectivity issues aren’t impacting every iPhone 18 Pro Max user, but they do appear to be relatively widespread.

Interestingly, the problems appear to be exclusive to the iPhone 18 Pro Max, which uses a Qualcomm modem. The iPhone 18 Pro, which uses Apple’s C2 modem, is seemingly unaffected by these AT&T connectivity issues.

Are you an iPhone 18 Pro Max user facing connectivity issues with AT&T? Does iOS 27.0.1 fix the problems? Let us know down in the comments.

Update 10:50 a.m. PT: In a statement to MacRumors, AT&T emphasized that affected iPhone 18 Pro Max users should update to iOS 27.0.1. The carrier added that it’s working with Apple to solve the problems. Apple also released an AT&T carrier settings update today.

title: Apple TV unveils new series reuniting stars of record-breaking comedy
snippet: Apple TV announced a new comedy series coming—The Choir—that reunites Ruth Jones and James Corden, the duo from beloved UK sitcom Gavin & Stacey. more…
fullText:
Apple TV announced a new comedy series coming—The Choir—that reunites Ruth Jones and James Corden, the duo from beloved UK sitcom Gavin & Stacey.

The Choir is new Apple TV series from Ruth Jones and James Corden, reuniting the ‘Gavin & Stacey’ duo

Last year reporting indicated that Apple had struck a deal with Ruth Jones and James Corden for a new comedy series.

Now Apple has made it official: Jones and Corden are reuniting for The Choir, a new Apple TV series coming in 2027.

The duo might not be as well known to US viewers (though Corden has an established US track record), but they starred together in the massively popular UK sitcom Gavin & Stacey. For context, its series finale in 2024 became the UK’s most watched scripted show ever.

Here’s the official series summary for The Choir:

Brother and sister Ben (Corden) and Lisa (Jones) haven’t seen each other for several years. Ben has been living abroad, while Lisa has carried on in their small English town, where nothing ever happens. But when events take a sorry turn, Ben is forced to return to a life he never wanted, a town he never liked and a family from which he’s estranged. Can the unlikely healing of a rift with his big sister come in the form of a struggling local choir and the ensemble who sing their hearts out each week?

Guest stars include Hannah Waddingham, James McAvoy, and Jim Broadbent, and there’s a strong supporting cast too.

Apple describes the show as being a comedic drama about “family, friendship, love and music,” with a seemingly similar heartwarming feel to that of Gavin & Stacey.

Are you a fan of Gavin & Stacey? Is The Choir of interest to you? Let us know in the comments.

title: Googlebook gets Luminar photo editing app with ‘Continue On’ support
snippet: One of the biggest questions around Googlebook is what app support will look like and, as the platform officially arrives for customers this week, Luminar is debuting a rebuilt photo editing app for Googlebook. more…
fullText:
One of the biggest questions around Googlebook is what app support will look like and, as the platform officially arrives for customers this week, Luminar is debuting a rebuilt photo editing app for Googlebook.

Luminar is a photo editing app that’s available across desktop platforms like Mac and Windows, but it’s also on Android, iOS, iPad, and ChromeOS. Now, it’s also making the jump to Googlebook.

The Luminar app has been rebuilt with support for Googlebok OS and meets “Tier 1” quality standards for the platform including keyboard shortcuts, resizable windows, drag-and-drop, and more. 

That’s on top of Luminar’s existing Android support for photo editing which includes the ability to adjust qualities of your photo, handle RAW edits, and use AI for features such as swapping out a background, masking, and more. You can even start edits on your phone and finish on your Googlebook as Luminar supports “Continue On.”

	

Luminar explains in a press release:

Luminar for Googlebook is fully adapted for large screens, meeting Google’s Tier 1 quality standards and introducing capabilities such as drag-and-drop, keyboard shortcuts, and resizable windows that weren’t previously available on phones and tablets. After several rounds of testing, Luminar has built a range of capabilities specifically for Googlebook OS:  

Built for the laptop: resizable windows, full mouse and keyboard support, shortcuts, hover states, multitasking, drag and drop, and file handling

New for launch: Generative Erase, HDR Merge, and batch editing – features usually associated with professional editing

One app, one subscription: use Luminar on an Android phone and on a Googlebook with the same account. [If available at launch:] With Continue On, you can start an edit on your phone and finish it on the laptop

Googlebook owners can download Lunimar via the Play Store. A temporary offer gives 12 months of access to Luminar for free, with a later one-time purchase unlocking the app’s premium features permanently.

title: Google details Gems to skills migration, including free access
snippet: As we spotted over the weekend, Gemini is replacing Gems with skills, and Google today fully detailed the migration. more…
fullText:
As we spotted over the weekend, Gemini is replacing Gems with skills, and Google today fully detailed the migration.

The news today is that skills are now available in the Gemini chat experience after debuting in the Spark agent. These reusable instructions for common tasks can be invoked with a / command from the main prompt box instead of having to launch via the Gem manager. This offers a more unified experience in the long run.

Example skills include preparing for presentations, matching writing styles, and getting different perspectives.

Skills will gain feature parity with Gems over the coming weeks. This includes the ability to share skills with others using links, and adding Google Drive files or notebooks for context. 

	

Gemini will automatically migrate Gems to skills, with the new feature available for all free users who don’t have Spark. 

Personal Google Accounts will lose access to Gems starting in November. The migration will happen for Google Workspace business, enterprise, and non-profit customers in March 2027, while education users have until June 2027.

Skills start rolling out today to Gemini chat users globally. All other customers can expect access in the coming weeks.

title: Google Acknowledges Day 1 Android App Performance Issues on New Laptops
snippet: Five new Googlebooks are available now, but the company says that not every Android app will offer “smooth performance” at launch.
fullText:
If you were planning on buying one of Google’s three new Intel-based Googlebooks, it might be worth waiting a bit. The search giant told Android Authority on Monday, launch day, that certain Android apps may not run smoothly right away.

“The vast majority of Android apps run smoothly across both Intel and Qualcomm Googlebooks right out of the box,” a Google representative said in a statement. “Because many Android apps were originally designed for Arm chips, a handful of complex apps or games need some developer tuning to run their best on Intel-based platforms.”

It’s unclear what complex applications Google is referring to, or if any of the Play Store’s most-downloaded apps are among them. It’s also unknown just how many Android apps are affected.

			

More from CNET

A Google representative did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Not all five of the new laptops will face this issue. The three affected Googlebook models, manufactured by Lenovo, Acer and Asus, are built around Intel’s Panther Lake architecture. The two Googlebooks manufactured by Dell and HP contain Qualcomm’s Snapdragon X Elite chips, which are natively compatible with Android-based apps. The Qualcomm-based Googlebooks likely won’t have any issues running the full breadth of apps available in the Play Store.

The performance issues with the three affected models are not entirely unexpected. Intel silicon is not immediately compatible with Android software, just as Qualcomm’s Arm-based Snapdragon X chips are not optimized for Windows. 

These issues might persist for a few generations of Intel-based Chromebooks before they are fully fixed. Google previously said on its developer blog that running Android-based apps on x86 silicon results in reduced performance and battery life, since the Arm code needs to be translated in real time.

That incompatibility could pose a challenge for Google and some of its partners, since the Googlebook lineup was marketed as premium laptops meant to unify ChromeOS, Gemini AI and the full library of Android apps. If there’s a performance hit on any of the most popular apps, the promise that you’ll be able to move seamlessly between working on your phone and computer starts to fall apart.

“While the potential for app incompatibilities is something to be aware of, it’s not a huge cause for concern unless you’re considering a Googlebook for mission-critical work,” said CNET Managing Editor Josh Goldman. “If there’s an Android app that’s an absolute must-have and you’re concerned, you should contact the app developer to check for compatibility before you buy one of the Intel-based models.”  

The first wave of Googlebooks is now available. The cheapest available model, manufactured by Acer, starts at $899. Configurations from other Google-partnered manufacturers start at $1,299. Every Googlebook is packaged with one year of Google AI Pro and Nvidia’s GeForce Now cloud gaming service, as well as three months of YouTube Premium and Adobe Photoshop.

title: Gemini for Android Auto is just giving up on answers for some drivers
snippet: The promise of Gemini for Android Auto is huge, as the AI assistant is theoretically more capable than Assistant was. But, as it’s now becoming the only option, a weird issue is leaving Gemini for Android Auto perhaps less than useless, as it just gives up on answers from drivers. more…
fullText:
The promise of Gemini for Android Auto is huge, as the AI assistant is theoretically more capable than Assistant was. But, as it’s now becoming the only option, a weird issue is leaving Gemini for Android Auto perhaps less than useless, as it just gives up on answers from drivers.

To say Gemini’s launch on Android Auto has been riddled with issues is a bit of an understatement. For months users have reported problems with various commands and just overlooked bits of functionality. I’m personally still waiting on Google to fix the issue where Gemini just keeps on talking or waiting for a response after I’ve completed a task via the touchscreen instead.

A new issue popped up this week, though, that’s not only frustrating, but just a waste of time.

Users report that Gemini for Android Auto is hearing commands, processing them, and then just giving up entirely on the answer. A Reddit user shared a video of this and several others chimed in with the same problem, and it’s one I’ve also personally encountered just this week. 

	

	

The issue doesn’t seem to have anything to do with signal strength or the question being asked. Gemini just sits there thinking for a few moments before giving up.

The video above demonstrates the issue when paired to a Pixel phone, but users report the same issue when paired to Samsung and Motorola devices too; I’ve noticed it with my Galaxy Z Fold 8. Google has, so far, not acknowledged the problem as far as we’ve been able to find.

Are you running into this problem?

title: Watch F1 on Apple TV tonight, free for everyone in the US
snippet: The Bahrain Grand Prix is streaming for free on Apple TV this weekend, subscription not required. Rather amusingly, the location of the Bahrain Grand Prix is actually in Sepang, Malaysia. Usually, F1 on Apple TV requires a paid subscription. But this weekend, it’s free for everyone to tune in. You can catch up on qualifying in preparation to stream the live race tonight, which kicks off at 3 AM Eastern Time. more…
fullText:
The Bahrain Grand Prix is streaming for free on Apple TV this weekend, subscription not required. Rather amusingly, the location of the Bahrain Grand Prix is actually in Sepang, Malaysia. 

Usually, F1 on Apple TV requires a paid subscription. But this weekend, it’s free for everyone to tune in. You can catch up on qualifying in preparation to stream the live race tonight, which kicks off at 3 AM Eastern Time.

All you need to watch is to get the Apple TV app on a compatible device, be in the United States, and stay up late enough to watch live. 

Coverage starts at 1:50 AM Eastern Time, with the race scheduled to start at 3 AM Eastern Time. You can of course watch later on-demand, if you’d opt to go to bed at a reasonable hour. 

You can get the Apple TV app on Apple devices, Amazon Fire Stick, Roku, PlayStation, Xbox, Android and more. You can also watch in a web browser at tv.apple.com. 

With qualifying happening earlier today, Red Bull’s Max Verstappen has snatched pole position for the first time this season, with Lewis Hamilton taking second and championship leader Kim Antonelli in third. It’s Red Bull’s best chance at a race win so far this year.

You may be wondering why the Bahrain Grand Prix is being hosted in Malaysia. In a normal year, the Bahrain GP would have happened much earlier in the season. But due to the ongoing Iran war, the race was cancelled and the Bahrain organizers instead decided to sponsor a race elsewhere in the world instead. 

Despite not being part of the official F1 calendar anymore, Sepang is a fan favourite circuit that should make for some exciting action on track. 

Again, use the Apple TV app to tune in for free, no subscription required. The race starts at 3 AM Eastern Time, with broadcast coverage starting at 1:50 AM.

title: Google Home now lets you preview Nest Doorbell ringtones, just in time for the holidays
snippet: Smart doorbells usually center their features around their security features — person alerts, motion tracking, the works — but they also go a long way in making your front door a little more fun. Google is no stranger to seasonal doorbell chimes, and ahead of a few months packed with holidays, the company is making a big improvement to how you setup your doorbell ringtones. more…
fullText:
Smart doorbells usually center their features around their security features — person alerts, motion tracking, the works — but they also go a long way in making your front door a little more fun. Google is no stranger to seasonal doorbell chimes, and ahead of a few months packed with holidays, the company is making a big improvement to how you setup your doorbell ringtones.

As part of today’s Google Home update, you can finally preview the chime you’re assigning to your Nest Doorbell from within the app itself, saving you the hassle of having to stand in front of your own door to hear it for yourself. Home now includes audio previews for both standard chimes and limited-time holiday themes, making it easy to know exactly what spooky sound — or Christmas jingle — your visitors will hear whenever they arrive.

Unfortunately, you’ll still need to wait for those timed offerings to be available throughout the year; only Oktoberfest is currently actively available under Google’s doorbell theme settings. Still, our own Ben Schoon is already seeing the play button active and available within the Home app for both seasonal and classic themes, with a play button available to the left of every option.

You can find this option within the Doorbell theme menu under Doorbell camera settings in the Google Home app. If you’re anxiously awaiting some Halloween tones as October rolls in, however, you’ll need to keep waiting. Meanwhile, the Oktoberfest sound ends its annual run on October 9th.

title: How to Disable Some Apple Intelligence Features on Your iPhone or Mac and Reclaim Valuable Space
snippet: The new AI features could be taking up a lot of storage on your device.
fullText:
Apple launched iOS 27 and MacOS 27 in September, and those updates introduced a revamped Siri AI powered by Apple Intelligence to Apple devices. While the new Siri was better at most tasks in my testing, it can still take up a significant amount of on-device storage space. On my iPhone, for example, it takes up about 6.4 GB of data, while it takes up about 17.9 GB of space on my MacBook Neo.

If you aren’t using the new AI features, you can disable some of them, and depending on what system you’re on, you can reclaim some of that valuable storage space. That way you can stave off for a little while the dreaded pop-up that tells you your storage is full – I need that extra storage for photos of my wife, son and dog.

		

			

Here’s how to see how much storage Apple Intelligence is taking up on your devices and how to disable – or at least limit – it on different operating systems. And don’t forget, Apple Intelligence is only available on certain devices.

How much space is Apple Intelligence taking up on your device?

How much space Apple Intelligence is taking up on your device is easy to check. If you’re on iPhone, go to Settings > General > iPhone Storage > iOS. From here, look for the Apple Intelligence tab to see how much space it takes up on your iPhone.

On a MacBook, click the Apple logo in the top-left corner of your screen, then go to System Settings > General > Storage, and click the i next to MacOS. A new pop-up will open to show you how much space Apple Intelligence uses on your MacBook.

Disabling Apple Intelligence on your iPhone that’s running iOS 27 or later is straightforward. Go to Settings > Siri > Turn Off Siri and follow the on-screen prompts. You can then go back and check your storage, and Apple Intelligence should be gone from that menu.

Disabling Siri AI can free up a few gigabytes on iOS 27.CNET

If you’re running iOS 26, you can disable Apple Intelligence by going to Settings > Apple Intelligence & Siri and tapping the toggle next to Apple Intelligence. This should free up some space on your iPhone.

You might also have to disable other Apple Intelligence features across your iPhone. To do this, go to Settings > Screen Time > Content & Privacy Restrictions and tap the toggle next to Content & Privacy Restrictions. Then, tap Intelligence & Siri. From here, you’ll need to tap into Image Creation, Writing Tools and Intelligence Extensions and tap Don’t Allow in each one.

This should free up a few gigabytes of space on your iPhone.

You can free up a few gigabytes of space in iOS 26 by disabling Apple Intelligence features.CNET

How to disable Apple Intelligence on your Mac

Disabling Apple Intelligence and freeing up storage space on your device can be weird, depending on which operating system you’re using. For instance, if you’re on MacOS 26, it’s easy to disable the feature and free up space. If you’re on MacOS 27, it’s a little more complicated. 

We’ll start off with the easy one. To disable Apple Intelligence on MacOS 26, first click the Apple logo in the top left corner of your screen. Then go to System Settings > Apple Intelligence & Siri and click to toggle next to Apple Intelligence. That should free up a few gigabytes of data on your device.

Disabling Apple Intelligence on MacOS 26 frees up a little bit of storage.CNET

There are a couple of potential ways to disable Apple Intelligence on MacOS 27. The easiest way I found to free up a few gigabytes of space is to click the Apple logo in the top-left corner of your screen, then go to System Settings > Siri and change your language to something like English (Irish). Siri AI isn’t available in every region yet, so changing your Siri language to a language from one of those regions could trick your device. Granted, it freed up only about 4 GB for me.

I changed my Siri language, and it freed up a few gigabytes of space.CNET

CNET’s sister site PCMag has a more in-depth way of turning off Apple Intelligence and freeing up some space. However, I couldn’t get this method to work. I’m not sure why I couldn’t get this method to work, other than that my device is running MacOS 27.0.1 and not MacOS 27. Maybe this will work for you, though.

According to PCMag, you have to go to System Settings > Screen Time > Content & Privacy. Then, toggle Content & Privacy off. Click Siri and change it to Siri Classic. Then go through the list of Capabilities and turn each feature off.

You’re not finished yet. Then, go to System Settings > Siri and select Don’t Allow Siri or Siri Classic.

Finally, you’ll need to go into individual Apple Intelligence settings and disable those features. Some easy ones include going to System Settings > Notifications > Summarize Notifications and turning the toggle off, or going to System Settings > Messages > Settings and turning off Message Summaries.

You could do all that work, or you could just switch your Siri language as I did. The choice is yours.

For more iOS news, here’s what to know about iOS 27 and iOS 27.0.1.

title: Apple reportedly planning second wave of product announcements later this month
snippet: MacRumors reports that in addition to Apple’s expected event on October 13, the company is planning to unveil another batch of new products in the final week of the month. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
MacRumors reports that in addition to Apple’s expected event on October 13, the company is planning to unveil another batch of new products in the final week of the month. Here are the details.

New Macs and OLED iPad mini expected before year’s end

Over the weekend, Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman claimed that Apple will, in fact, hold an event on October 13 to announce “its long-awaited smart home hub with a screen, the new HomePod mini and an updated Apple TV.”

Gurman’s report came amid uncertainty over whether Apple would hold an event or announce the new products through videos and press releases, as it has done in the past. Gurman had previously said only that Apple would unveil these products on October 13, without specifying how they would be announced.

In addition to these three products, Apple had also been expected to unveil a new OLED iPad mini and new Macs, including an updated iMac and a touchscreen OLED MacBook Pro, both powered by an M6 chip.

Now, MacRumors says that, “according to multiple sources familiar with the matter,” the company will unveil another round of new products in the final week of October.

The report stops short of saying which products will be announced. It also does not provide a specific date, or say whether Apple will hold a second event or unveil the products through videos and press releases.

That said, these announcements at the end of the month would cap off an unusually busy October for Apple, with the iPhone Duo launching on October 23 and the company also expected to report its quarterly results before the month is out.

title: Emmys will move from broadcast TV to Prime Video in 2027
snippet: Non-Amazon Prime subscribers will be able to watch the awards show on the platform.
fullText:
In Brief

Posted:

7:37 AM PDT · October 6, 2026

Image Credits:Ashish Vaishnav/SOPA Images/LightRocket / Getty Images

		

							

											
									

					

	

Amazon announced on Tuesday that Prime Video will be the new home for the Emmy Awards, marking another major Hollywood awards show’s move from broadcast television to streaming. This will also be the first time that the ceremony has had a dedicated home, as the show rotated across broadcasters like ABC, CBS, Fox, and NBC over the past seven decades.

Prime Video will stream the awards show worldwide for six years for free, starting in 2027, where it will go live in over 240 countries and territories. Non-Amazon Prime subscribers will also be able to watch the awards show on the Prime Video platform.

The terms of the deal were not disclosed.

The move comes as the Emmys face potential viewership declines, as more of its audience moves to streaming services. This year’s ratings for the 78th primetime Emmy Awards on NBC were down nearly 10% from the year prior, after a couple of years of growth, the AP reported. However, the telecast’s 6.87 million viewers this year were higher than its all-time low of 4.3 million in January 2024.

The Emmys aren’t the only major awards show making the shift to streaming. Last year, the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences announced a deal giving YouTube the rights to stream the Oscars beginning in 2029, while Netflix has streamed the Screen Actors Guild Awards since 2024.

Samsung is today officially launching its new Galaxy Tab S12 series with the Tab S12+ and Tab S12 Ultra delivering big displays, powerful specs, and some new software tricks too.

Available starting October 7, the Galaxy Tab S12+ and Galaxy Tab S12 Ultra continue Samsung’s flagship tablet series with some nominal upgrades. While they’re visually almost identical to prior generations, there are some spec bumps, including the new MediaTek Dimensity 9500.

Besides the size, one of the notable differences is that there’s no cellular version of the Galaxy Tab S12 Ultra. Samsung has no smaller screen size available this year, with the Galaxy Tab S11 still serving as the 11-inch option.

Both tablets, Samsung says, include a larger vapor chamber for heat dissipation, retain the IP68 dust/water resistance rating of prior models, and ship with One UI 9 (Android 17) out of the box with seven years of OS + security updates. There’s also an S Pen included in the box, with a keyboard cover and other accessories available as add-on purchases.

	

Samsung has new partnerships with productivity apps, too. Adobe Photoshop is pre-installed on the Galaxy Tab S12 series. The app has S Pen optimization and users get four months of free access to the app as well. Notability, a recent arrival on Android, is also pre-loaded and comes with a six-month trial. There are further freebies in Goodnotes, LumaFusion, Notion, and others, as well as a six-month Google AI Pro trial for boosted Gemini capabilities.

Galaxy Tab S12+ starts at $1,199, while Galaxy Tab S12 Ultra starts at $1,399, the latter being a $100 increase over last year. As mentioned, both are available in the US starting October 7.

title: Type One Energy raised $200M to build a fusion power plant by 2034
snippet: Type One Energy is betting that its lean approach to fusion power will get a power plant on the grid faster, and investors have rewarded it with $200 million.
fullText:
Type One Energy, a Knoxville, Tennessee-based startup founded in 2019 to build fusion power plants, announced Tuesday morning that it has raised $200 million from investors.

The funding helps the startup move up the ranks of the top-funded fusion power companies. But fusion is a costly field to work in. It sits at the cutting edge of plasma physics, materials science, and advanced computation, and even $200 million doesn’t always go far.

Even so, the new Series B should get the company halfway to paying for a 400-megawatt commercial power plant, Type One CEO Christofer Mowry told TechCrunch. If Type One can bring it online by 2034, he added, the company could complete its first power plant using less capital than many of its competitors, even with one or more subsequent rounds of funding.

The secret, Mowry said, is Type One’s business model. The company will design the power plant and many of its components, then turn to a “bespoke” network of suppliers chosen for the project to build them, he said. Most fusion startups rely on suppliers for some components, but Type One plans to go further.

That approach keeps costs down. “The amount of capital that we need to raise to commercialize fusion at Type One is just a different order of magnitude than if you were going to be vertically integrated,” Mowry said, referring to companies that make most of their own parts in-house.

“Why would I want to spend on bricks and mortar?” he added. “I used to run a big nuclear manufacturing company. That’s expensive.”

The fusion startup has already started assembling a roster of partners. Type One will build its first two fusion devices on the Tennessee Valley Authority’s Bull Run site, and infrastructure consultant AECOM is working on engineering for Infinity Two, the initial commercial power plant. Competitor Commonwealth Fusion Systems has licensed its high-temperature superconducting magnet technology to Type One, and the technology will help form the backbone of Type One’s reactor design.

By relying on outside suppliers, Type One becomes what’s known as an integrator, a company that assembles a product from parts made by others. That minimizes its own risk from activities like manufacturing, but it introduces a different kind of risk.

The upside is access to partners that may have more expertise in certain areas, like AECOM, the infrastructure consultant working on Infinity Two. “They have 10,000 people, most of them are engineers of one kind. We’re never going to have 10,000 people,” Mowry said.

The downside is that integrators have less control over their suppliers than an in-house team does. The most famous recent example might be Boeing, which relied on Spirit AeroSystems to supply fuselage sections for the 737 and 787 airliners. After a series of quality-control failures, including a door plug blowing out on an Alaska Airlines flight in 2024, Boeing bought Spirit, bringing it in-house to improve standards.

Type One is betting that it can manage the integration risk, and that it will be lower than the risk of doing everything in house. “These business models are successful because they let companies focus on managing risk and developing a high level of competency in their slice of the value chain,” Mowry said.

The round was led by repeat investor Breakthrough Energy Ventures and Clutterbuck Capital, with participation from Lowercarbon Capital, Siemens Energy Ventures, and SiteGround Capital. The company had previously raised $82.5 million in an extended Series A.

Tim De Chant is a senior climate reporter at TechCrunch. He has written for a wide range of publications, including Wired magazine, the Chicago Tribune, Ars Technica, The Wire China, and NOVA Next, where he was founding editor. 

De Chant is also a lecturer in MIT’s Graduate Program in Science Writing, and he was awarded a Knight Science Journalism Fellowship at MIT in 2018, during which time he studied climate technologies and explored new business models for journalism. He received his PhD in environmental science, policy, and management from the University of California, Berkeley, and his BA degree in environmental studies, English, and biology from St. Olaf College.

title: iOS 27 adds four new ways to customize your iPhone’s Lock Screen
snippet: iOS 27 continues Apple’s trend of giving you more control over the design of your iPhone’s Lock Screen. This year, there are new customization options, wallpaper settings, and more. more…
fullText:
iOS 27 continues Apple’s trend of giving you more control over the design of your iPhone’s Lock Screen. This year, there are new customization options, wallpaper settings, and more.

Extend wallpapers

iOS 27 brings new Apple Intelligence editing features to the Photos app. This includes a revamped version of Clean Up, as well as a Reframe. Another new option is Extend, which intelligently expands your image so you can adjust its aspect ratio, straighten horizons, or just add more space around the edges.

As seen above, the Extend feature also comes to the Lock Screen in iOS 27. If a photo doesn’t match your iPhone’s aspect ratio or isn’t cropped quite right for a wallpaper, iOS 27 will automatically suggest using Extend to fix it.

Extend will use AI to generate additional image content around the edges, so you have more flexibility when setting a picture as your iPhone’s wallpaper.

Generate your own wallpapers

iOS 27 brings big improvements to Image Playground, which is Apple’s app that lets you generate images using artificial intelligence. The changes to Image Playground also come to your iPhone’s Lock Screen. Now, you can generate wallpapers using Image Playground right from the wallpaper picker in Settings or on the Lock Screen itself.

In the wallpaper picker, you’ll see a new “Image Playground” option. The feature will create stylized versions of images from your Photos library, such as “Retro Illustration” and “Animation.”

You can also create a custom wallpaper from scratch just by describing what you want in natural language.

Move the clock

iOS 27 finally lets you shrink the clock on your iPhone’s Lock Screen. While Apple has let you customize the clock’s size for several years, iOS 27 goes a step further. Now, you can move the clock on your Lock Screen up to the top row of widgets.

This frees up space on your Lock Screen so you can see more of your wallpaper. It does, of course, come at the expense of being able to glance at the time from far away. For many people, though, the point of the Lock Screen is to show off wallpapers, and iOS 27 makes that even easier.

With iOS 27, you can now swipe away the Now Playing widget that appears on your iPhone’s Lock Screen. Even if you clear the Now Playing widget, whatever you’re listening to will continue playing.

This is great if you find yourself accidentally tapping the Now Playing widget on your Lock Screen.

Wrap up

title: Upgrade to Apple Watch Series 12 or Ultra 4? Here’s how to get the most out of it
snippet: Upgrade to a new Apple Watch Series 12 or Ultra 4? Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4 bring upgraded performance and new health sensing features. Still, they can feel like the same watch in day-to-day use unless you know where to look for the changes. From new health complications to automatic Shazam recognition, a few setup changes can help you get more out of your upgrade. Here’s what to try. more…
fullText:
Upgrade to a new Apple Watch Series 12 or Ultra 4? Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4 bring upgraded performance and new health sensing features.

Still, they can feel like the same watch in day-to-day use unless you know where to look for the changes. From new health complications to automatic Shazam recognition, a few setup changes can help you get more out of your upgrade. Here’s what to try.

Refresh your watch face

Start by adding exclusive new complication options only supported on the new Apple Watch models. Series 12 and Ultra 4 can display your live heart rate, steps count, and readiness score on your watch face.

You can add these complications to your favorite watch face to unlock new insight into your health and fitness. 

For me, live heart rate data has been an essential new complication, using a single slot with better data compared to the old wide slot with less current data. Step tracking has also been a big motivator for getting activity logged earlier in the day. 

And since readiness score can change throughout the day based on your vitals and activity, displaying readiness on your watch face can be a great tip.

And while it’s off by default, you can enable quick switching between watch faces with a swipe at Settings > Clock > Swipe to Switch Watch Face.

Turn on automatic Shazam

Your new Watch can identify music around you without a request to Siri or a tap on Shazam.

On Apple Watch, open Settings → Smart Stack and enable Music Detection. When you open the Smart Stack, Music Recognition can show the song title and artist.

It’s a small setup change with an obvious payoff the next time something unfamiliar plays at a restaurant or coffee shop.

Try Siri Modular

Siri Modular comes to every Apple Watch running watchOS 27, although Series 12 and Ultra 4 have more complication options.

Something I love about the Siri Modular face is how you can style it. For now, I have a few instances of the Siri Modular face in my rotation using different colors, fonts, layout styles, and complications.

Give readiness time to work

Adding a readiness complication is only part of the setup. You also need to collect the data behind the score.

Apple says to complete your Health Details, set up Activity and overnight vitals, enable Sleep, and wear your Watch while sleeping for at least seven nights. You also need sleep data from the previous night.

Find a charging window during the day so overnight tracking becomes easier to maintain.

So far, readiness has been an interesting experiment, but I think it’s still too early to call it useful for me. 

Daytime vitals

Lastly, the Vitals app has more insight with Series 12 and Ultra 4 hardware.

You can see daytime vitals, not just overnight, in the Vitals app. This is based on heart rate and recovery heart rate variability. Overnight vitals also factor respiratory rate and wrist temperature.

Looking ahead, there’s more to come for Series 12 and Ultra 4 with Siri Recap and Live Rewind on the way.

What are your favorite ways to get the most out of the new Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4? Share your ideas in the comments.

title: These are the best times to save money on your next flight, according to Google Flights
snippet: Ahead of the busy holiday travel season, Google is detailing the best time to book your next flight to get the best possible price. more…
fullText:
Ahead of the busy holiday travel season, Google is detailing the best time to book your next flight to get the best possible price.

With surging fuel prices have also come much higher plane ticket costs and, with that, everyone’s looking for a deal. In a blog post this week, Google Flights details the best times to book your next flight.

For domestic US flights, the best time is apparently 39 days prior to departure, but the lowest price can fall anywhere between 57 days prior and 22 days prior to the actual flight date. International flights should be booked much further out, with 89 days being the magic number there.

Thanksgiving and Christmas flights bend the rules a bit. Thanksgiving flights are actually cheapest 34 days prior to departure, but Christmas flights need to be booked much earlier at around 56 days.

	

Here’s the full breakdown from Google:

Domestic flights: 39 days before departure (low price range is 22–57 days)

International flights: 89 days before departure, but the average price drop during the low range (50–133 days out) is insignificant

Thanksgiving: Lowest prices hit 34 days before departure (low price range is 21–57 days)

Christmas: 56 days before departure (low price range is 33–67 days)

Spring break: 50 days before departure (low price range is 29–64 days) for trips in March or April

Summer vacation: 21 days before departure (low price range is 20–47 days) for trips in July or August

Trips to Europe: 49 days or more before departure

Trips to Mexico or the Caribbean: 43 days before departure (low price range is 24–69 days)

The post goes on to detail trending destinations for the 2026 travel season, with Hawaii being the top Thanksgiving destination and international trips to Greece and Canada trending around Christmas and New Year’s Eve.
